I'm a huge Dark Souls fan.
I'm a huge rogue-like fan.
Needless to say..I was very excited about this game.
It falls short just about in every aspect that makes those games fun.
Right off the bat, you kill a skeleton, and it drops a sword. Cool!
You kill another skeleton..its drops a sword. ...
The same Sword. Every. Time.
The combat is slow, and very unsatisfying.
I played the game for about an hour and didn't ever feel scared of losing my progression, because I hadn't felt like I'd actually progressed. The whole idea behind being scared to lose a hardcore character is the adrenaline rush and the need to actually function properly under pressure to keep your character alive..but you don't feel attached to your character in this game. If you die..oh well.
PROS :
Very unique art style. Think..Dark Souls + Windwaker, or something.
The music is awesome, and one of the main reasons I was drawn to this initially.
Rogue-Like with small progressions to make your runs not feel completely useless..the best kind.
CONS :
Boring, stale combat
Absolutely NO sense of progression
Every single mob type drops ONE weapon. Over and over and over.
Although the level design is cool, I was desperately hoping for a scenery change after not even an hour.
Someone mentioned this earlier.. the humor. I dig humor in games, don't get me wrong..but this just seemed..forced. I love corny humor when its placed in the right game..but this isn't banjo kazooie; pick a theme and perfect it instead of trying to do 10 things at once.
This game could potentially find its way to success if they revamp the combat and looting system.
Its sad that those were suppose to 2 of the biggest alluring aspects of the game, but they definitely fall short.
I almost wish this was early access, so I knew the devs realized this game wasn't finished.
Hope to see it fixed up in the future. For now, this wasn't worth my $30.

Although many people compare this to Dark Souls I still have no clue why. The closest thing you will find is the controls, however this game is its own thing.
This game can be played both Coop and Solo and still be greatly enjoyed, if you're one of those rogue-like players that want constant action. I'd say this isn't the game for you, combat uses the slow and strategical approach much like Dark Souls but much like 3D Zelda games such as Windwaker and Ocarina of Time.
So far in my 2 hours I have reached level 6, (I had to stop since I was uploading for people concerned over the game). I have not died yet and have had no trouble reaching there, the game rewards players that like to explore every nuck'n'cranny in the game before making progress by giving weapons that would otherwise be found on the next level. I wouldn't say I was dissapointed in the game, I have been following it for quite some time and was excited for finding another  rogue-like to enjoy.
I'm sure the game is much more enjoyable with friends (Something I have none of) and variety in playstyle is there, it is just not given to you at the start. To some the combat is clunky and slow, but compared to what it was it has been improved greatly. As stated the game is meant to be taken slow and strategically (As with the implementation of crafting, which is awesome btw). You can buy recipes from merchants for next runs, as well as buy dyes and find vanity armour for yourself. The only thing you lose is your weapons and materials, everything else from your armour, dyes and codexes you keep for life.
The art-style compliments the game really well, at times I'm taken by it and find myself admiring the landscape before going into combat.
However, I'd be lying if I didn't say I was dissapointed with the game being ported to console. This is a good thing for the developers but a rather middle-finger to the PC gamers that supported it in the first place, I do hope with the port they promise for further content. Instead of taking months on end to even adding additions to the game due to porting to console issues.
The game itself needs more variety in attacks rather than re-used animations, such as all greatswords feeling the same, all axes feeling the same, all straight swords feeling the same.
I doubt they'd do this, but a man can hope...
If you have a band of friends wanting to team up, I greatly recommend this game.
If you're the type that enjoys taking their time and exploring levels to find treasure, this is your game.
If you're one of the dozens that think this is a Dark Souls game, don't buy it.
It's not.
And never will be.

ABZU is such a beautiful game on a number of levels. It's Art Direction and Soundtrack are absolutely superb. The art, though low polygon in nature, is detailed and so well crafted that you can't help but admire everything that you see visually within the game. The quality of the animation is great too, the underwater wildlife and fauna feel so organic that it's heavy stylisation becomes invisible.
The music is an entire discussion on it's own. Both on a technical and artistic levels, ABZU's soundtrack is phenomenal. Your movements, your progress and each mechanic in the game feels like it's tied alongside the music which brings forth the emotion in what is essentially an underwater walking simulator.
Which brings me to my next point, this is a "walking simulator" game and for many people that may be an issue as it's both short, very linear and the gameplay is minimal. However I have to point out that even with this, that doesn't hinder it.
Though the game is short, coming in around an hour to an hour and a half of playtime, with no real replay value besides acheivement hunting, it doesn't outstay it's welcome. There are points in the game when the awe disappears and it starts to get dull, but a brisk movement forward takes you right intot he next section which swiftly keeps things moving forward. For an experience like this, I felt that the game was just the right length.
In regards to the games mechanics, they're very basic. The majority of the time you'll be swimming in this space and it's highly recommended that you use a controller to play. However, the controls aren't totally responsive and feels a little clunky at times, probably to make the underwater motion and animation feel more well paced and natural. There is some light puzzle solving, but nothing that you could consider to be difficult.
The real question lies in it;s value proposition. At £15, this game is very expensive for what you're getting out of it. It's incredeibly beautiful, the gameplay is okay but no amazing and you're only getting an hour and a bit out of it.
I'd highly recommend playing this game, but for most people, I'd suggest waiting for a sale.

My first impressions: this is a great, great game. It's not perfect, but if you like space strategy games, you need to play this.
Summary: a must have for a strategy fan. I don't like scores, too subjectives, but this is at least more than 8,5 and less than 10 out of 10.
Playing on: Win 7 64 SP1, i-7 4770, GTX980, 16GB RAM.
Liked:
-Stable, no bugs encountered, 0 problems so far.
-UI is much more polished, easy and beautiful than other Paradox games (EU games, CK games)
-Tutorial is fantastic, this is not Europa Universalis "tutorials" or "scenario tutorial", they have put a good work here (and it works...not like that scenario tuto from EU IV)
-Graphics are really beautiful and you can zoom in and out to see your stations or ships or even a planet just as icons or with a lot of detail. If you zoom all in to a ship, it will you remember Eve Online (less details, and ofc only if you have seen that game)
-Background music is nice, and some parts/songs are fantastic for a space game. I played all 4 hours with music on and i will continue to listen to it while i play, no doubt.
-Galaxy is HUGE. You can select a few options here to generate, but the maximum is 1000 stars. Yes, 1000. And maybe 5 times more with mods (but no mods yet, ofc lol) 1000 stars is crazy, and also fantastic for a Marathon game!
-Lot of customization options: races, planets, techs, names (you can name almost all in game, your stations, your ships, your planets and your leaders) I have seen no option for selecting the AI races in the game, maybe that option is not there.
-Lots of technologies divided in 3 main branches: physics, society and engineering and you need a scientist leader for each branch. They said about 300 techs in total, that's a good amount and i'm sure they will add more in future development.
-Resources and anomalies (events, more or less) to discover in the galaxy and some anomalies (events) lead you to a series of missions that you can do for some extra resources, techs and maybe more, i don't know yet.
-A nice ships editor where you can create your own ships with modular components that first you need to research, obviously. You can select different "bodies" for the specific ship you want to create that let's you add more small weapon mounts, or more medium mounts, or more slots for services, etc. If you are creating a service ship (like a colony one) you'll want more modules to put some extras, but if you want just a big ship to do damage, then you'll want the body that has more weapon slots. Each body has different visual little details that you can observe when zooming.
-I tried with 3 languages i know (more or less lol English, Spanish and French) and translations are vey good.
-Addictive and fun.
Disliked:
-There are no report screens for the income and expenses. You can pass the mouse over resources and a popup will tell you what are you expending in total (for instance, 50 credits in stations) but there is no extensive report to see exactly where are you expending to better manage your incomes. This is a basic in every strategic game and it's strange that Stellaris don't have better reports and more info.
-Apparently, you cannot create your stations like the rest of the ships. You can build one with a construction ship and then add modules for a military stations, but cannot modify scientific and mining ones.
-Just 2 win options: own 40% of the systems or kill/conquer all the other races. I'm sure they will add more (with a DLC? i hope no)
-Needs more visual customization for races and to distinguish one empire from other, apart of color of ships and flag icon (portraits of individuals at least). You can play againts 36 AI enemies, but there are just 6 species groups and one you have seen a molluscoid, you have seen they all. But, of course, this will come with DLC's.
-This game is going to steal a lot of time from my rest.
In summary, a must have for any fan of strategy. Fantastic.

I have a confession to make. I love all four of the "main" BUILD games. Duke, Shadow Warrior, Blood and Redneck Rampage all have their own unique character and style, despite being basically the same games with different art and sounds. The last two unfortunately seem to be owned by companies who aren't interesting in using what they've got, which is a shame. Despite Duke and SW both having their source code releases, we've had no such luck with Blood and RR. There are are a couple of exploratory games which are attempting to remake Blood, but without access to the source code, they just don't *feel* right. As as everybody knows, "feel" is very important with an FPS. So, the only way to play Blood for now is through DOSBox.
Luckily modern computers are powerful enough to run DOSBox without a glitch, so Blood can now be played faithfully on near enough any x86 based machine you want. Which is good, as Blood is amazing. Whilst Duke is based on guns'n'muscle action movies and SW is schlocky kung fu, Blood is low-budget gory horror movies. So think... Evil Dead 2 - The Game. That's about what we're dealing with. So, your character quotes one-liners whilst kicking a zombie's head across the graveyard. You can use an aerosol as an improvised flamethrower, set people on fire with flare guns, and wield two guns at once, Woo-style. This is not a game that takes itself seriously.
The level design is wonderful, with plenty of variety in locations - my favourites being the "house of horrors" secret level, and the train from the first Episode. Sound design is well done as usual, with the cultists spouting a conlang made for the game, and nice atmospheric music.
Unfortunately at this point the Build engine was starting to show it's age, and some of the graphical workarounds don't really work - particularly things like the train cars. Still, it's fun. And that's what's important.

When I started playing this game, I was about 9 years old. This game litteraly was my childhood, but I could only play the trial version and only while I was at my grandparents house. Now that I am 20, and have my own computer, I have decided to pick up the game for nostalgic reasons. After playing it, I was once again hooked. This is the type of game to get if you are looking for a challenge while also just walking around and cutting someone down or fireballing them to death. Now that I am older and know how to play strategically, I have made myself a Mage that regens more mana than I use.
The game definitely is geared to make you constantly have trouble clearing a floor, but the harder the enemy, the more xp you get, so it balances itself out. Besides, who would want to play a game that is easy to beat? The game also incorporates a special On-Death question. It gives you the choice to revive on the spot at the cost of XP and Fame (my least favorite option), Revives you at a "Nearby Level" for a Cost (It can send you lower in the dungeons), then finally you can choose to drop ALL of your money and be sent 3 levels up in the dungeon (Provides you with a speed run challenge to get your money back), oh and if you aren't fast enough, your money will disappear. Isn't that awesome?
As for graphics, you shouldn't expect very much. The game was released in 2005 and hasn't had any graphic updates that really CHANGED THINGS. But as for me, I do not care if the graphics aren't that of the newer games coming out these days. You can see what is going on and you dont have any trouble understanding what is what.
Story? There isn't really a story to go by other that: "After many days of travel, you've reached the forest town of Grove. ABZU is such a beautiful game on a number of levels. It's Art Direction and Soundtrack are absolutely superb. The art, though low polygon in nature, is detailed and so well crafted that you can't help but admire everything that you see visually within the game. The quality of the animation is great too, the underwater wildlife and fauna feel so organic that it's heavy stylisation becomes invisible.
The music is an entire discussion on it's own. Both on a technical and artistic levels, ABZU's soundtrack is phenomenal. Your movements, your progress and each mechanic in the game feels like it's tied alongside the music which brings forth the emotion in what is essentially an underwater walking simulator.
Which brings me to my next point, this is a "walking simulator" game and for many people that may be an issue as it's both short, very linear and the gameplay is minimal. However I have to point out that even with this, that doesn't hinder it.
Though the game is short, coming in around an hour to an hour and a half of playtime, with no real replay value besides acheivement hunting, it doesn't outstay it's welcome. There are points in the game when the awe disappears and it starts to get dull, but a brisk movement forward takes you right intot he next section which swiftly keeps things moving forward. For an experience like this, I felt that the game was just the right length.
In regards to the games mechanics, they're very basic. The majority of the time you'll be swimming in this space and it's highly recommended that you use a controller to play. However, the controls aren't totally responsive and feels a little clunky at times, probably to make the underwater motion and animation feel more well paced and natural. There is some light puzzle solving, but nothing that you could consider to be difficult.
The real question lies in it;s value proposition. At £15, this game is very expensive for what you're getting out of it. It's incredeibly beautiful, the gameplay is okay but no amazing and you're only getting an hour and a bit out of it.
I'd highly recommend playing this game, but for most people, I'd suggest waiting for a sale.

I came into this game expecting what the game page described and was honestly let down.  I wanted to like this game but it's honestly quite boring and feels like a cheap sci-fi, medieval knock off of Dark Souls.  I love rogue-like games but this just doesn't do it for me.
Pros:
-Very pretty artistic design.
-Good music.
-Lore can be found in dungeons.
-Co-op with friends.
That's about as far as pros go.
Cons:
-Story:  I wouldn't say this game has much of a story as much as it is simply talking to a illuminati like character (it's a giant pyramid with an eye) just telling you to go into the dungeon.  He comes off as a narrator and in my opinion, the writing was terrible.  The game comes accross as a "serious" type dungeon crawler but he keeps saying things that are supposed to be humorous but comes off as silly and dumb.  He gives you quests at the beginning of each dungeon which are alway along the line of "kill this many enemies".
-Stamina system: Stamina will regen but the bar of max stamina you can hold will permanently decrease until you eat food which will restore a portion.  This would not be a problem if not for the fact that it decreases every Charged strong attack or every 2nd charged normal attack.  Monsters drop items to craft food but it just seems to become a monotonous cycle of kill>get items>craft food>restore stamina.
-Combat:  It just feels wonky and not smooth at all.
-Empty levels:  Although this game has beautiful artistic design, the levels all just feel empty and the same.  While it is randomly generated you keep seeing the same props laying about with no real use.
-Enemies:  There really isn't much variety and they all drop the same items and have the same weapons.  The map feels spammed with level 1 enemies that are easy to dispatch.
Over all, this game just seems like an incomplete early access game and is not worth $30.  If you're still determined to buy it however, I urge you to at least watch gameplay before your final decision.

Originally released in 1997 for the Sony PlayStation, Final Fantasy VII is a favourite of many. In 1998, Squaresoft ported Final Fantasy VII to PC, including 'remastered' music. The original port was riddled with bugs, the only 'real' improvements where grammar fixes and the ability to play in up to 800x600 resolution (this only improved the 3D rendered assets, so most backgrounds where stretched). This PC port however features even higher resolution (even the cinematics are higher-res!) and as you may have read, cloud saves. This re-release could have been alot more, I was expecting mouse support when I first launched and high-res backgrounds. You can probably mod the game to add such features, but it's not the games graphics that make it good, it's the story! Featuring a well-written story with many twists and an absurd amount of lore, this version of the game is definitely worth the price as modern games rarely come close to matching this games quality of writing and the amount of side quests. While the game was a slight let down in what I had come to expect from a PC release, the story does more than make up for it, and for that, I recommend it!

Blood is a fps developed by Monolith back in 1997. The story, as you would expect for a typical 90’s shooter is not of significant importance. It is as far-fetched as the overall theme of the game. You control a gunslinger, once worshiper of a demonic occult who was betrayed and killed by the dark God he was worshiping, now somehow resurrected he seeks revenge.
The game is split into episodes, as it was common in those days. Through short cinematics at the end of each episode you get the progress of the story . From the  start of the game the horror and violent themes are easily noticeable. There is a lot of graphical violence and gore blended with comical aspects quite successfully I have to say. Also for a game that came out in 1997 the work on textures and lightening effects is quite impressive with the level designers packing as much detail as possible in most of the environments. In some aspects the game was really ahead of its time, like for instance the destructible environments. Most of the things can either blow up or be set on fire. However as the game progresses the strong themes of the first two episodes decline which is really a shame because there are several memorable levels in the game. The atmosphere in general is what makes this game unique and distinctive from the other doom clones of that era. The music fits perfectly with the art design as it gives a mysterious and a dark tone to the overall creepy theme.
The player has to choose from a big arsenal of weapons with unique and creative functions. There is also a secondary fire mode which was quite original at the time as it is actually a useful installment that offers diversity. However many of the weapons are weak and are just there for novelty purposes. One of the biggest flaws of the game in my opinion is its insane difficulty. Some of the enemies not only are brutally overpowered but they also have pinpoint accuracy and even at the medium difficulty settings you must be ready to die many times. It will also take some time to get used to the throwing mechanics but once you do there is nothing more entertaining than lining up a bunch of enemies and lighting them on fire or blow them up with a dynamite.  There are also some issues with the mouse aiming. Installing the bmouse application helped a lot but still, the mouse movement, especially the vertical axis just doesn’t feel right. I had to tweak it a lot to make it work decently with the rest of the movements.
It goes without saying that Blood isn’t a perfect shooter obviously. It has a somehow limited appeal which is not to be taken seriously, an unforgivable difficulty level and many other flaws but aside that it is a solid old school shooter which delivers non stop action and mindless fun.

*Now, to give this review context, I need to explain something. I am NOT a 'Bloodite' or particularly a fan of any of the 90s FPSs as most of them were from before my time. However, I'm not exactly ignorant to games such as Half Life, Deus Ex, Unreal Tournament, Timesplitters, etc. So it's not like I favor today's overglorified rail shooters over the classics.
I'm saying this, because my major criticism for this game may be overlooked or even laughed at by people who enjoy games such as Doom, Strife and... Noah's Ark 3D.
Anyway, that disclaimer aside, this game's control scheme, for me is unplayable. I can't make sense of it, at least not for very long. I'm not sure, since I don't have much experience and this may have been a pretty standard control scheme for the time but it's dated to say the least. What bugs me is that there's no way to change the controls yourself, which is fine, I don't need to have to map out the buttons myself, so long as a functional alternative control scheme is provided. They really should have added one in the steam release as a patch, I don't see that being too difficult to be honest.
The control scheme makes this game feel prehistoric for me and I found that the only way to progress through the game was to save, every time I cleared a room. This is mainly because I'm used to the modern standard of WASD to move and this control layout just throws that out of the window and encourages you to use the arrow keys, something that I was always taught NOT to do growing up.
However, in spite of this, I still enjoyed the game. It's bright, colourful, fun and I'd be a liar if I said that the concept of playing as an undead cowboy who likes to sing show tunes whilst redecorating the walls with other people's entrails didn't appeal to me. I was always interested in this franchise and I was quite happy to see that this game came out on Steam and that it was in the sale at the time.
I know that I must have enjoyed the game, because in spite of the crippling control scheme, I stuck with it for hours, until I got really deep into the game. However, dying over and over again soon got old, shooters like this are only fun if you get a flow going and no momentum can ever be kept up, so long as you get killed off, because your brain is trying to play Half Life and accidentally pressed the button to make Caleb pull his trousers down.
I understand that some people might be thinking 'well, don't play it like you would a modern FPS, embrace the old school control scheme' but that's not possible. I was able to do that and get into the zone for a while but it's like trying to fly a plane, when you only have a driver's licence. Yeah it's the same in theory but once you take off the rules completely change. I know that the knee jerk response would be to say 'well you can play a range of FPS games, so why can't you play this?' Well, to rephrase your question to fit the analogy, 'well you could drive a car, so why can't you fly a plane?'
Overall, I'd recommend Blood to anyone who knows what I'm talking about and laughed at my feeble attempt to understand a control scheme, that was probably being designed around the time that Harvey was premiering at the pictures but anyone else, I'd say that I'm not exadurating, with my complaints on the control scheme.
If you're unsure, I'd get this in the sale as I would say that it's worth your time, if you're able to play it, even if you're only able to play it really badly like I am but if you struggle with regular FPS games, then I doubt that you have much hope with this one.

It's also too difficult to tell what sets an enemy off, how far his range of hearing is and all that. You can get ambushed by enemies from the other side of the map  for killing a single dude in a room one time, then another time you might not alert guys standing in the next room. Just wanted to share my thoughts, since this game is already rated so highly I don't feel the need to go indepth in what makes it work in spite of the problems... It's a good game that's worth picking up at least in a sale, I just think it could've been much better.

Dust: An Elysian Tail is amazing! I loved it and I enjoyed every moment when I played it.
In this game, we play as Dust who doesn't remember anything. With Ahrha, a talking and magic sword, and Fidget, a cute nimbat, the three will go on a journey together, fighting monster all around. And so... Dust's quest has begun. The story is quite interesting, especially near the end and the truth is revealed.
As for the game itself, that's a good 2D platform game, and we explore beautiful and mysterious places. The music in this game is fantastic, it's just... So beautiful! I especially love the music in the glade, the first place we explore after the intro. There are also many sidequests to do, and we can get many rewards like item, money and experience. Battles are pretty neat as well, using your sword and combining your attacks with Fidget in order to crush your ennemies. Think it's possible to get a combo of 1000? Well, we some training and skills, it's definitely possible. There are also some challenges and many treasures to find, so, it you love exploration, go ahead and enjoy the music and background while you're exploring. There are many references and cameos from various others games.
As for the difficulty, well, I played the game twice, once in the normal difficulty and once in the hardest difficulty. Difficulty is quite reasonable though, in the hardest difficulty, it was challenging and I died a few times too. So, this is good somehow, it's not too easy, not too hard, that's perfect.
Now, the game is more or less short, only five chapters (with a prologue) and four bosses. But there are many places to explore and many sidequests to complete as well. Hmm... I have the feeling the game miss something, I kinda wish they were more somehow, I don't know what does it miss though. Oh well... And who knows? Maybe we'll have a sequel and I wouldn't mind at all. Anyway... I'll definitely recommend to play this game! ^^

This game doesn't get fully reviewed by me. I'd rather wanna tell you why I quit it after 6 minutes of gameplay and never touched it again. It's hard to bore me, it's hard to get me to quit a game because of it's graphics, gameplay or story. What gets me to do that is poor execution at the top of its class.
First off: The game could be great. It really could be great. Sure, it's a bit like a ripoff of Doom but still. It's an old FPS with a nice atmosphere. And the graphics are nice, too. I'll say it again: it could be a good game. But...
How do I put this? Remember what happened to the classic Doom games when they got on modern systems and such? Right: they received updates to enhance performance and controls. Blood doesn't have that.
In Blood, you control the whole game with your keyboard. No mouse support whatsoever. I mean come on! Even Doom could do this.
Controlling a game with only your keyboard wouldn't be too bad if it wasn't an FPS. To control an FPS without a mouse and just, for instance, the arrow keys, is a chore. And in this game it sure is a chore. It's a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥to control your movements or to aim up or down.
Then there's the resolution settings. It is set to 800x600 by default. If you're like me and your monitor isn't from the 80's you'll be weirded out if trying to set the resolution any higher, even if the option is there. Why? Because if you set the resolution to, for instance, 1280x1024, instead of a full screen experience in a higher resolution you get tons of miniature screens packed side by side and you can't see anything. Not that it matters anyway, it's just so damn pointless.
Aside from that the little bit of gameplay I experienced wasn't all too good either because the enemies are frickin' bullet sponges (at least in the starting area) and, because of the wacky controls, it's hard to hit anything and your ammo is depleted quickly without you even hitting an enemy.
To conclude:
The controls are horrendous. It may have rebindable keys but playing an FPS with just your keyboard is excruciating. This one little thing♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off so much that I can not recommend this game since it's next to unplayable if you want to have a decent amount of fun and don't wanna waste time turning around for an hour and a half because it doesn't have mouse support.

A unique game unlike any other. An unexpectedly wonderful and addictive time. The music is pretty great too.
They had overflowing creativity with a lot of their game design (such as a banshee miniboss that makes you go deaf. in a rhythm game. really.), traps that would speed up / slow down music, and their overall punny bosses (rhythm chess, anyone?).
Let alone you can import your own music as easy as picking the files you want for each stage, and also the mod support, such as the megaman conversion mod, showing that fans will be able to keep this game going for a long time.
Playing this reminded me what it feels like to get that exciting new game when you're 5 years old again.
Playing this reminded me what it feels like to be happy.
Fully recommended.

This is more of a neutral, "I don't want to bring the game down because of my ignorance so I'm not rating it badly" review.
I guess whenever I see the word "Roguelike" I immediately think the game will be an RPG unless it's just vastly different in all aspects. This game is
. My bad really, I didn't read the description well enough. If you're looking for an RPG roguelike, then I have to say look elsewhere.
Even though it looks like it would be the perfect RPG game, the only thing they have that is remotely close to this are codexes, which are perks basically that your successive characters earn, but that's it. The only difference your character will make through their playthrough is based on the weapons/equipment they will use, so really this game is item based, in that you need better items to become stronger.
Unfortunately the items are only separated by tier level (Tier 0, Tier 1, etc) so it makes it difficult to tell beyond the tier level what exactly each item does. Item description are short and really do nothing beyond telling a joke. Seriously there's no info on each weapon, just some tid-bit that the developers thought would be funny. I would consider this a pretty big con, but your opinion may vary.
Besides that the game is great to look at. I actually really like the art style and the heavy use of triangles. It gives it a unique look. The combat itself is very smooth and flows easily in my opinion. I had no problem with that. I'll just get bored with the game if there's no RPG elements (levels, stats, classes, etc), which again, is my bad for not picking up on.
If the game looks fun to you then pick it up. I will be refunding it because it wasn't quite what I was expecting, but I'm sure it will be fun for those who don't need an RPG.

ABZU is such a beautiful game on a number of levels. It's Art Direction and Soundtrack are absolutely superb. The art, though low polygon in nature, is detailed and so well crafted that you can't help but admire everything that you see visually within the game. The quality of the animation is great too, the underwater wildlife and fauna feel so organic that it's heavy stylisation becomes invisible.
The music is an entire discussion on it's own. Both on a technical and artistic levels, ABZU's soundtrack is phenomenal. Your movements, your progress and each mechanic in the game feels like it's tied alongside the music which brings forth the emotion in what is essentially an underwater walking simulator.
Which brings me to my next point, this is a "walking simulator" game and for many people that may be an issue as it's both short, very linear and the gameplay is minimal. However I have to point out that even with this, that doesn't hinder it.
Though the game is short, coming in around an hour to an hour and a half of playtime, with no real replay value besides acheivement hunting, it doesn't outstay it's welcome. There are points in the game when the awe disappears and it starts to get dull, but a brisk movement forward takes you right intot he next section which swiftly keeps things moving forward. For an experience like this, I felt that the game was just the right length.
In regards to the games mechanics, they're very basic. The majority of the time you'll be swimming in this space and it's highly recommended that you use a controller to play. However, the controls aren't totally responsive and feels a little clunky at times, probably to make the underwater motion and animation feel more well paced and natural. There is some light puzzle solving, but nothing that you could consider to be difficult.
The real question lies in it;s value proposition. At £15, this game is very expensive for what you're getting out of it. It's incredeibly beautiful, the gameplay is okay but no amazing and you're only getting an hour and a bit out of it.
I'd highly recommend playing this game, but for most people, I'd suggest waiting for a sale.

If you are a fan of hardcore games with rogue-like mechanics then Necropolis is a game which you like. In this game death, which is permanent and you lose your progress, is a major part. To prevent that you have to increase your combat skills and your know how of the game. You will die and each play through you will learn something useful.
There is no deeper story in that game, you play it because the gameplay.
Necropolis is a third person action-role-playing video game. It takes places in a netherworld with moving platforms and hidden treasures. You can compare it to Dark Souls but much harder because if you die, it is permanent and after your respawn the levels are different every time. Death is by the way a major part of the game. It is the challenge not to die and that is hard. There are many traps and monsters with different abilities which want to kill you. So a main part of the gameplay is to increase your skills that you don’t die.
With the Unity Engine Necropolis has a very unique and minimalistic art style, like a cartoon, it reminds me of the graphics from The Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker. It’s difficult to say that the graphics are good or bad but it is a fact that Necropolis has only little details. Positive with these art style is that the game is always clear with an awesome overview within fights. In addition to that you have a minimalistic but beautiful user interface, I like that. In conclusion I can only say that Necropolis has beautiful with a nice little UI, but you have to like that style.
Jon Everist already composed the Music for Shadowrun which is a great soundtrack and also Necropolis has a very awesome music, it fits perfect and builds a diabolic atmosphere.
Every run is different from the others because the levels are random generated. That also means that you can't really prepare yourself for the next time if you die. This feature makes the game a lot harder but I like that because every run is interesting and never become boring.
You can play coop with up to four players which can be fun and easier but also annoying and harder than you expect because in coop friendly fire is always on. It's important to be careful where you strike your blade. Coop is a completely different experience than single player and that increase the fun of the game.
Necropolis is a hard game and if you die, it is permanent. You can compare it with Dark Souls but it's very different. This game is much harder and does not forgive mistakes. Dark Souls is in comparison to Necropolis just an easy mode. If you don't like Dark Souls give Necropolis a chance, I hate it but I love Necropolis. Are you ready to die? Then get it and take the challenge.

Gonna get a lot of heat for this but here it goes: I love Mafia 3. True, the gameplay is lackluster, however the carefully crafted tone and overall feel of the game itself carries a weight that puts the majority of momentous titles of this genre (and those outside of it) to shame.
When Mafia 3 was released I got my copy early for that I preordered (which is something I almost never do) the 3rd instalment of this series months prior. However due to technical dificulties what were partially because of the atrotious optimisation rendered the game unplayeable for me until now. I've never been happier that I've waited for long.
Following a year after it came out Mafia 3 has changed drastically as far as I can tell. Glitches were mostly dealt with, every DLC are now available and each enjoyable (short but sweet). And about the base game, well... Though it still suffers from graphical issues as well as glitches it runs smootly. Though you're forced to do the same activities over and over the gunplay is satisfying. And let's be real, who played the OG Mafia or Mafia 2 because they wanted to play an FPS? Shooting is a secondary objective, the story is the primary focus, that's where Mafia 3 shines the brightest.
Unconvential is it may be for a game that's supposed to be about the life of mobsters it takes another route and provides a unique take on the genre. The downside: it's another revenge story. The upside: it was done right by astablishing the protagonist's relations with other charaters' first.
It's cinematic but not in the way Ubisoft like to label its games. When watching a cutsceen you truly feel like watching a movie with the help of wonderful camerawork and subtle nuances such as the 4:3 image ratio, great use of filtering, graining and distorting both the audio and the video during scenes that were made to look like archived footages. Movie buffs are gonna live for that aspect.
When talking about the story there must mention of the actors too. The performances are top of the line, hands down the best part of the game. Rick Pasqualone is back at it again as Vito and he's as good as ever. Alex Hernandez is perfect as Lincoln. He portrays him as a likeable brute with a brain and a heart. You never know what's on his mind and dispite his actions he always means well. And of course there is Lane Compton, a newcommer to the series and I believe it's his first time appearence in a video game. He plays John Donovan and he does it so well I could write a bloody long essay on that character alone, but I better not, this review is long enough anyway. :D Long story short: give that man more roles, he's freakin' talented and is also a sweetheart, just check out his Twitter, you'll see what I mean.
Also wanna add a quick sidenote: Mafia 3 uncovers more than one aspect of raceism, something that in most games as well as movies and on telly usually surves as a cheap plot device, however here the writers doesn't shove it in the players' face but uses subtle touches mixed with brutal honesty to reinforce its point. Very brave step dealt with in a delicate way.
And of course there is the music and the setting and I could go on and on 'till you grew tired of me praising the hell out of a product that is half-baked and in some ways unpolished. Hell, I didn't even enjoy Mafia 3 at first and had to learn to accept its flaws and like it. Still, it pains me to see how others undeservedly bashing it when it's actually truly good and how much better it could have been with the missing features added to the core gameplay.
Kudos to everyone at Hangar 13. You guys did well, not perfectly, but I see bright future ahead of you so don't give up. Looking forward to seeing more from the studio and hoping that the publisher won't rush releasing anything unfinished.
~ Cheers,

This may well be the best space strategy game I have ever played.
Basically, you take Distant Worlds Universe; take out the annoying features; improve the graphics and accessibility; and add the modding that i would like to have seen in Distant Worlds. And there you have Stellaris: superior to Distant Worlds in almost every respect, except perhaps the private fleet (which may well be moddable).
What makes this game really awesome is the moddability. Don't like the decisions made by the designers? Redesign the game to your own liking. Want to play in the Milky Way galaxy? make your own galaxy (or wait for someone else to make it).
Stellaris as released is a very enjoyably game, and I would recommend it even without the moddability. But Stellaris is so much more than that: it is essentially a tool for creating a space game that plays exactly the way you want it to. It doesn't get much better than that!

Asthetically, everything holds up. The art style is consistent througout and sound effects are clean and punchy. The problem unfortunately comes from gameplay.
My first and most prominent gripe is the dribbling system, or lack thereof. Slide tackling gets old pretty fast as you get pummled from every angle and with no penalty to the opposing team. It feels impossible to manouver anywhere in which an opposing player is standing due to the risk of getting tackled by a 10 yard slide. Getting rid of the ball ASAP seems to be the name of the game.
In a previous match, a challenge encouraged me to tackle 10 players without sliding (blocking tackle). I managed to do so but immediately after completing the challenge, I went right back to using sliding as my sole means of performing a tackle. There's little argument to justify using a blocking tackle.
Power ups are pretty cool but theres only 6 and they seem pretty unbalanced. A rather infuriating one is an electrocuting drone which lasts much longer than any other power up.
The challenges add some needed variety to the game although they can go from being mildly challenging to feeling down right impossible. You can collect stars and coins but the menu options and guide don't provide any direction as to what they mean or if they can even be used.
I've complained enough so let me reassure you that there are some good points to this game. Shooting feels robust and the abilitiy to switch between manual and auto passing on the fly is great. There's plenty to like about this game but the minor annoyances mentioned above are likely to put you off playing this one often.
If you have a few controllers and like to play with friends, or maybe you're looking for a cheap and causal game to play, breaking your usual FPS routine, this might be the one for you. Just make sure you don't pay too much for it as you'll likely get bored rather quickly.
Message to devs:
This game is so close to being really well polished. Keep working on it!

It is like an older simpler version of Europa Universalis 4, but you have Knights instead of advisors to give you bonuses or carry out your will! I wish I had found and played this amazing game earlier.
Knights of Honor is like EU4 a fairly slow paced real time game (there are buttons for speeding the game up though) where diplomacy and interpeting and manipulating the worldwide opinions and events is very important. You can make Trade, Non aggression pacts, Alliances and Royal marriages. Peace and War are of course present and can be declared however you wish, but breaking Trade/Alliance/Royal marriage carries penalties.
Spies are present and can do all sorts of shenanigans if you are so inclined and they work in a rather unique way, or you can fill your royal court with Army carrying Marshals and forget spies, merchants or any other utility Class your knights could choose and just crush your enemies, stomp out rebellions until they calm down, and intimidate your enemies with your massive armies so they will be too afraid to try to stop your quickly expanding realm while plundering everything in sight so you don't run out of food and money.
A lot of the countries you can choose to play as has unique units that you can recruit anywhere the resources are present at and the locations of provinces determines what other local units might be around for recruitment, Vikings for example are available as special local units for hire in Scandinavian provinces.
Combat is handled either personally or by the AI, heading in yourself can be preferable if the armies are about equal in strength and you want to ensure victory by say sacrificing your cavalry to rush and kill the enemy marshal, ending the battle unless a reinforcing marshal is present for them. While fun, you can generally trust the AI to handle battles where you outnumber and/or outclass the enemy, except when terrain or castles or such are about to mess things up.
In addition to your knights you have your royal family that you should take good care of, marrying off your women to secure peace and making damn sure you have male heirs so succession is not a problem.
Finally there are multiple ways to win, so far I have only managed to get the Kingdom Advantages win, which is gathering all the trade goods and acquiring all Kingdom Advantages which are bonuses to various areas of your Kingdom obviously. There also Click Here to Claim victory buttons where you demand others to recognize your greatness and undisputed rule, and independant somewhat irregular meetings to determine a Supreme Ruler.
Gonna try to conquer Europe as the Golden Horde next with hordes of horse archers. And after that play as a muslim country and cover the world with Camels.

Fully recommended.

The gameplay is really stiff and cartoonish, ragdolls are stiff and pre-animated, and the melee fights are really boring. The streets are empty and its makeing me depressed.
The A.I is horrible. People keep respawning the same places, everyone takes the same route and uses the same covers. It's predictable and really repetitive.
The driving mechanics are by far the worst thing I've experienced so far, everything is wobbly and you keep drifting - there is no chill to the cartoonish driving mechanics. It feels like they spent more time creating the driving mode, then they did on the A.I. Whenever I drove in the game, I had to turn down the volume, because the drifting would be constant and loud. Not to mention the screen shaking when drifting/turning, it's really weird and it kept giving me a clunky
"Dutch Angle" view, really never wrecking when you have to turn multiple times and not crash into something.
The guns feel bad, really bad. You've given an oversized crosshair, that makes all the bullets feel like they are 80mm (though it also seems like they hit in the full circle, even with aim-assist disabled). The worst part is, you can only carry a limited amount of weapons, and that's just really a poorly constructed mechanic. Every time the mission ends, you start on a new one, losing all your weapons, ammo, grenades and adrenalin shots. This is tedious since there's no way you get to free roam the city.
The police are nearly non-existent. You can go around, kill random people for 10 minutes and nothing will happen. It's boring. The only way to get police to chaze you, is to find a random passing officer, and smack him or a citizen around. So after you do that, and the police finally arrive, they greet you with instant bullets - there's no arresting or anything - not only does bullets fly after and around you, but instantly 10 police cars spawn, driving full speed at you, so there's no time to react. It feels so forced since the police are none existent in the city, but when you finally get them to chase you, it feels like the city is made up of nothing but police officers.
The escape mechanic for the police is also horrid. It's a circle you have to escape, love that though, but the fact you can escape it in less than a second, and make them completely forget about you, is garbage.
The graphics are really terrible. The city is "full of "details" (buildings with loads of things plastered to them), but nothing that doesn't look plastic - the lack of a destructive environment makes it really boring, and the textures aren't that rich. I feel like the environment could have gotten a little more sound to make it feel a bit more alive because the game does feels really dead.
Everything feels scripted - the passive NPC animations and the dialogues.
The menu is the worst menu I've experienced in 2017. When you have to select DISPLAY options to change the graphics -
- you have to watch every single menu option pass through your eyes, flashing like a screamer on your screen.
This gets really annoying looking at, after exiting the menu, just to re-enter it, because something broke or the FPS dropped too low; just to go all the way back the DISPLAY options, to change something, and then do it on repeat for about 6 times. Pure seizure material.
It takes about one-point-five (1.5) seconds to reach the other end of the screen with the "quick-select" option (if you can call it that), but might take longer with a lower FPS.
Overall, I don't like the game, and I don't find it to be fun. Feels like the developers wanted an easy buck.

Stellaris is one of those loved 4x games by Paradox Interactive and starts a new series set in space. And like most Paradox games it lacks some major aspects and some parts seem poorly conceived.
But I do know Paradox and I do know that the next major patches and DLCs will bring the game to a point of awesomeness. But right now I kind of regret the hours I spent playing this game.
The early game phase is fun with all the quests and exploring but gets boring after you've seen it multiple times. The midgame lacks most. There is nothing to do but wait for technologies and get a working infrastructure while fighting some really boring wars. Also the war system lacks some major decisionmaking and war objectives.
But most of all the sector system is somewhat annoying. I try to handle my new colonizied planets for a while myself before handing them over to the AI but a major downside is that you can't have special ressources getting used by your sectors if those aren't mined in the defined sector itself. You can trade over the whole galaxy but not get your own special resscources to your own sectors. Also you can give credits and minerals for quick development but not take 'em out again. Also why am I only able the get 75% of the ressources produced by a sector and not 100%. Once a sector is fully grown you lose 25% of your ressources just by having a sector. I could handle the fact that a sector would cost credits to maintain because one leader can handle an unknown number of planets (I can only handle 5 without further technologies) and so you don't need to have one for every planet but you'll have abundant credits and minerals in the midgame anyway 'cause of the lack of things to buy. It seems like the developers don't want us to handle colonizatios ourselves. Best to let them get handlet by the AI as soon as you get them.
But nonetheless. It's a 4X game, it's a Paradox game. I love EU4, i love space and I will spend way to many hours playing this game. If you can work with the mentioned issues and some really bad performance issues with great fleets it's worth playing even now.
What I liked most was the nation creation tool. Even with the flawed color system.
So let's hope  we will get some fixes soon and the DLCs won't be as overpriced as the latest  EU4 ones.

This game is amazing. I thoroughly enjoyed GC2 and this one is definitely an improvement in my book. All told I'm a huge fan of the 4X genre, especially sci-fi. I got it on sale a couple weeks ago and I've already spent a bunch of hours in this game cus it truly is addicting. To be honest I can't really put my finger on it. There isn't really one thing that GalCiv does well. Somehow the combination of mediocre components is what makes this game something I truly do love to play.
Now, there is A LOT of room for improvement but I think that makes this game even better. The tech system is probably the best system implemented but there are still some small bugs to work out there. Mostly just wrong descriptions or assigning upgrades to an unrelated tech.
The diplomacy system has improved in many ways compared to its predecessor. However, it does have some flukes in it. For instance, the way treaties work needs some extra clarity. like when I add an exploration treaty on my side it increases the worth of my side even though from what I can see it allows me to view their forces as well. The exploration on their side is the same except it increases their side's worth. Its mostly just small things really.
The biggest thing IMO that needs work is the AI. right now they are horrible at planetary management and war. The Drengin empire can outnumber my ships 4 to 1 and I'm still able to invade half a dozen planets before they even give a fight.
The approval system is also in need of some love. From what I can see so far it is basically just a battle between your empire size and population of the planet decreasing it, versus entertainment centers and other things increasing it. Incorporating a tax system like its predecessor had would be nice and perhaps adding a debuff to approval when the planet has enemy vessels nearby or something to give it depth.
Overall, StarDock has done a good job so far in my book. They have shown that they are still devoted to this game post-release so I look forward to future updates.

What a wonderful game continuing the story of Geralt of Rivia. My favourite aspect of the game is how wholesome and real the characters feel. Never have I laughed out loud so much playing a game, and that is thanks to some of the amazing quotes from Geralt and co. I would even say playing the game through to completion the second time is better than the first, because I made completely different decisions to my first run through, and i discovered completely different parts of the story I hadn't seen first time though. This game is all about choice, and your choices and past greatly affect the outcomes of the story, even more so than the previous installment in the series. Another aspect I really liked was that I could link my saved game from the previous Witcher game to this one, so that the important decisions I made in the last game carried over into this one - sometimes my past haunted me! The combat has greatly improved in this installment and I enjoy nothing more the running and killing some beastie of bandit with the wonderful sound as my blade cuts a few organs. The game can also be quite complex, juggling potions, oils, armour upgrades, traps and magic as well as Geralt's swords, which I only properly appreciated on the second run through on a higher difficulty, where you really have to use them all. The decisions in the game are really difficult, it can be really hard to tell who are the liars and who are telling the truth - on many occasions I got caught out. Hence playing it twice through makes it all the more interesting! Overall, a colourful, wonderful, beautiful game that makes me want to read the books it is based on, at least to see if my decisions were the ones Geralt actually makes!

Is the game good? Yes. It's a flawed gem of a game and one that could well have been one of the best RPG's ever made, if it wasn't for one thing: the combat. The combat is either shallow and dreadfully easy on "Easy", or absolutely impossible on "Normal". "Normal" is really hard mode and they need another difficulty in-between.
Putting that aside, pretty much everything else in the game is good. Graphically it looks very pretty when maxed out for a game this old.
Having never played Witcher 1, I found it's not very beginner friendly with regards to the story - but then I kind of expected that anyway. Nevertheless, if you have not played the previous game, expect to be confused... a lot. When you finally get your head round it you will find it has significant depth and is highly engaging.
Your companions all have back stories of their own and they are well fleshed out. Not many games have had me caring for characters I have only spent a minimal amount of time with in game, but this one got me!
The RPG elements are solid and allow for quite a bit of customisation. It has an interesting potion mechanic, based on your "toxicity level", so you can't just swig every potion you have before a fight.
So, all in all, it's a good game. It could have been brilliant if a few issues were resolved. Regardless of which, it has made me want to get Witcher 3 this February, so consider me hooked!

Back around 2006 to 2008 I played the heck out of this game. It was released during a time when no one was really making ARPG's anymore. You had Diablo 2, several years old at that point, Titan's Quest, and not much else. One of the few good games to come from publisher Wildtangent, I sunk many hours into this game and beat it multiple times with different play styles.
You can play as a summoner, as a mage, as a warrior, ranger, or any hybrid really, because there are no classes, simply skills and attribute points. It is actually a very open ended system that lets you make different kinds of builds.
While it definitely does not hold up today against modern titles like Torchlight 1/2, Path of Exile, Grim Dawn, and others it is still a good diversion for fans of the genre who want to experience something new.

While I haven't played this game for incredibly long yet, I would recommend it.
The combat, while slow and somewhat light-feeling due to a seeming lack of hitstun compared to games similar (See: Dark Souls) is still enjoyable and deliberate.
Graphically, it's quite simple and easy to look at, but at times can be somewhat dark and difficult to see in. This doesn't prevent you from being able to tell what's going on, but definitely reduces the clarity of a situation sometimes.
The atmosphere of the game is pretty nice.
It blends a strange, somewhat sarcastic and dry sense of humour with a dark and somewhat threatening dungeon. While I personally enjoy that, I could definitely see it being a negative for other players, as it occasionally takes away from the serious demeanor of the story (or whatever story you come across). Adding on, the music helps set the tone for the game. It's a very quiet, sharp sound that plays as you stumble across treasures and monsters in the dungeon. I like it. A lot.
Controls are pretty tight and easy to pick up if you've played a Dark Souls game. Things aren't explained very clearly past the first few seconds of staring at a controller layout, but the mechanics are relatively easy to pick up as the game goes on.
While the game is marketed as difficult, I honestly have not found much difficulty thus far! This could be due to previous experience with this genre of gaming, or it could be that the game itself is undertuned. I've seen a few reviews stating it was too difficult, and a few reviews that it was too easy, so take that how you will. It could be different for everyone.
As it stands, the game seems a bit unpolished and a bit unfinished, but still an enjoyable experience for the price.
You'd definitely be able to pull an easy 30-40 hours off of this game, and if the co-op is enjoyable/actually works, then this game is easily something you could come back to for a long time.
Co-op update: The netcode is alright, and the game runs fairly well with two players so long as the host has decent internet. The difficulty doesn't really scale well but it's enjoyable. The friendly fire mechanic isn't nearly as bad as I expected it to be, and you could play around it fairly easily within half an hour of playing with friends.

Before Torchlight, there was Fate. A dungeon-crawler RPG where you slay hordes of monsters, help the townsfolk and get items, gold and fame.
Pros:
1. Diablo-like: As my favorite RPGs of all time is Diablo, this game brings a very similar gameplay.
2.  Dungeon levels: while some seem very short or very long, the layouts, theme and monsters were pretty awesome and never boring(in my opinion)
3. Items are pretty basic but dual-wielding Wakizashis was super fun
4. Pet companions: Being able to load up your pet and send it town to sell your abundance of junk items for gold was very resourceful. Not to mention having a 2nd source of damage if you got surrounded
5. The music in this game was pretty chill and welcoming. Though I would've preferred some rock or some metal
Cons:
1. While the pet companion was helpful, the lack of selection was pretty sad. Cat or Dog is nice but would've been epic to walk around with a wolf or even a Falcon.
2. While being to change your pet into whatever monster by fish, I was really sold on the idea. Seemed like a waste of time to just sit at a fishing hole, trying to find those rare fish that give permanent changes or huge stat increases. It just wasn't my cup of tea.
Overall, this game is super fun, child friendly as there isn't really anything gory or inappropiate for younger ages.

Blood is a great game. This release, however, is not. Even for $5 this DOSBOX rerelease just isn't worth it. You have to do a lot of tweaking on your own just to get mouselook working properly, and then there are still problems with framerate, music, other controls, resolution, and the steam overlay. Everything is a hassle and it reeks of cashgrabbing and laziness.

The game's biggest problem is that the combat just isn’t satisfying. I swing my sword and there is zero weight behind it, the animation looks unnatural, and it just feels wrong. There are no transitions between animations, and this leads to the game just looking bad. The game's issues are not limited to this through unfortunately.
I played through the first level and tried out a few different weapons, I have no idea if there was any difference beyond aesthetics for some of them. Did the others that had different movesets do more or less damage? I have no idea. Not that I have anyway to judge how much damage I’ve even done to enemies. Sometimes if you hit them enough they kind of lumber over, not that it looks satisfying or prevents you from just wailing on them.
To address the appearance of the game, when I first launched I thought I had to change to my native resolution because the text was so blurry. But no, it was indeed the correct resolution. Also in the first level at least there are pottery items and barrels that look just awful. They honestly look like place-holder assets. Other than that the world in general is good looking, as is the protagonist.
Also the game isn’t funny. It makes consistent jokes that are misplaced, not humorous and just inappropriate to the setting. Is it trying to do black humor? Did the developers find this funny? I have no idea.

For folks looking for space exploration and empire builders, the 4X crowd, this is your holy grail.
Early game focuses on exploration, charting, and colonization with strong barriers blocking the normal early-game colony rush.  Science and discovery is as important as raw resource might in this phase and adds endless charm and uniqueness to each game.
Mid game transitions into one of diplomacy and early warfare as you and your neighbors establish a pecking order.  Exploration still occurs but the sites are dwindling by this point.
Late game moves into vast empires and federations staking claims and rearranging neighborhoods all over slights big and small.
Add to this late game crises (extra-dimensional invaders for example), relic ancient empires vastly beyond your starting capacity, nascent and emerging low-tech races, and a rewarding tech system you have a game that breathes fun and freshness in every play through.
Personally, this is what I've been waiting for nearly 20 years.
It was worth the wait.  And even more so now with the post-release improvements!

Well it`s clear that the game wanted more to be a "The Godfahter  meets Vice City" mix  than a proper sequel to the first 2 entries in the series. This didn`t end up quite as one would expect as the game was rushed and it is clearly not so well optimized and still a little buggy. One more thing that adds up to that is the fact that the collectibles are pretty much worthless.  But it did some things very good, and those are : the story, the setting(the atmosphere of the era and soundtrack are really at least on par with what Vice City managed at the time of its release) and the main missions(closer to linear games, but they work very good in this game).  The combat is decent, the cover system is good, the weapons feel nice for a third person shooter, but the stealth system suffers from lack of choices. You basically don`t have other options than stabbing and a silenced pistol. You can`t use the enviroment or take hostages, it really gets boring as you won`t get to see too much different animations as well. So, as long as you use the "weapons blazing" alternative, the gameplay is good. The DLCs are cool but kind of short. They do add some new gameplay elements and locations but unfortunatelly usless outside of the DLCs(even the weed growing as you really don`t need money in this game, you get your weapons everywhere and there are medkits in almost every corner-shop). It`s worth it though.
TLDR : Buy this game on sale, you should really give it a chance for the things it does good.

Played this game for the first time last night and ended up playing for 6 hours straight (it says I only played it for 5 minutes but I don't know why it's not recalling my previous time).  I should have gone to bed earlier, but it was very enjoyable.  It has a helpful tutorial that gives a good overview and feel without overwhelming with detail.  The art is beautiful, the different elements of managing your kingdom are well chosen and engaging.  There is a good balance between strategy and improvisation.  Really got me excited about the "grand strategy" genre.  It's evident that a great deal of care went into the design of this game.
I think right about the time I started to figure out that I could try negotiating royal marriages with other kingdoms and that would affect diplomacy and future implications about contingent succession, all happening on the side as it were in a game that I had been treating more like a Risk/empire-building game, that is when I began to feel very impressed.  The dynamic of different religions and occasional religious events and the subsequent effects that can have on every nation is richly complex and fun.  Espionage with different branches of possibilities and control.  The ability to choose auto- or manual battles.  Skills and experience bonuses.  Special trade goods and resources.  Kingdom advantages.  An excitingly reasonable diplomacy engine.  Reasonable morale.  Kingdom modifiers.  The different relational dimensions go on and yet it doesn't feel heavy, rather it was pretty easy to just dive in and start making waves.  Oh, I dig it!  Two thumbs way up!

Writing this review over a year after this game released makes no change in what my opinions were, and still are.
If you own an older graphics card, don't even bother getting this yet, Hangar 13/2K are yet to optimize this (still) terrible port. In my case, I get the same fps at all quality levels and options (around 40-50), with v-sync off and frame limit set to "unlimited". I have tried many fixes for this problem, but the game just isn't optimized for pc.
Overall, I think this is an interesting addition to the Mafia Trillogy, taking the series to 60's era New Orleans is not a place many games take you. The architecture and just the map in general is beautiful, when you can actually turn your camera without losing 20 frames, and the driving (although being a little hard to master) is my favourite of the series. The progression gives you choice (albeit not much) as to how you want to continue, such as if you want to kill the racket bosses to earn an upfront sum of money, or keep them alive to work for you and earn more in the long run. The story is captivating, at least I think so (I'm articstically-blind, so don't trust me on that one), but the ending was kind of weak.
Overall, I'd rate this game a 6/10. It would be 7/10 if not for the concurrent problems the game is still facing over a year after it's launch. But let's let the handy median work it's magic....

This game looks wonderful and has a great soundtrack.  The voice actors and actresses bring their A game.  You can see videos of outtakes and recording sessions on YouTube.  The two leads make a great team and I hope to hear them in other games together soon.
The hero and sidekick, Dust and Fidget, compliment each other really well.  Fidget is more than just the usual comic relief you get in most games, she uses projectile attacks which work in tandem with Dust's melee assault.  The higher your combo chain, the more bonus EXP you'll get from each battle.
Dust:AET supports the standard modes of play, keyboard, keyboard and mouse, or controller.  I am just at the end of my first playthrough using a controller, no real issues to speak of.
This game is also available on the Xbox 360 if you don't have a PC that can run it.  If anything, I strongly recommend at least trying the demo there.  This is a pretty solid game that offers more than many bigger budget titles have over the last few years.  I'm putting it on my list of favorite games.  I'm not sure where on that list just yet, but it deserves a spot.  Couldn't recommend this game more, play it now.

The classic aRPG from the same developers as Torchlight. I played this game when it first came out, and picked up the Steam copy later on. This is a pseudo-port to more modern PCs. The cartoony graphics hold up well. It's a fun little loot-fest, though not terribly deep. It has good difficulty options, and is basically color-blind friendly. However, it's mouse-and-keyboard controls only, and mouse is absolutely required. Controls are not remappable, and there's no included switch-access. Sound is a good fit for the game, but doesn't provide any information. Anything spoken by the narrator is also presented as text, so one just misses some ambience without sound.
It's infinitely replayable thanks to procedurally generated maps and the descendent character new game, although if you enjoy it, you'll likely just move onto the next game in the franchise.

It's awesome. It's just really good and really fresh. Spelunky meets nethack meets DDR... but don't play with the ddr pads unless... well, maybe that'd be cool too.
The music is excellent, as it would have to be for this type of game. One review suggested that it was hard but fair, and I couldn't help but feel that was correct. If you learn what things do and have even moderate situational awareness, you can get out of stuff. It's about getting into the groove and staying there, and that's what I was looking for.
The story-line stuff seems lightly added in, but that's ok. It doesn't detract from anything, and it's nice enough. The graphics are pixel, but that's trendy these days, and fills me with nostalgia, my other preferred opiate. The control sensitivity is very tolerant, but I think that's a bonus. the persistent upgrade mechanic is nice and engaging, without feeling at all grindy.
So yeah, I'd say this game was worth $10 easy, and I'd give it a strong reccomendation. You should probably buy this game, even if it's not your usual style, because this is gaming history, and it's actually very good. If it is your style of game, you should already have bought it instead of reading yet another positive review!

Necropolis is quite different from other games because of the fact that there are no checkpoints or saves. It's a Dark Souls type of game except that it doesn't have any bonfires or saves as you would call them. You have dodging, parrying, timed attacks, stamina management, sorcery, shielding, mobs of enemies, and big monsters. If you die, you can kiss your progress goodbye. That being said, here's my review.
It's a great game for people who are looking for a challenge. It takes all of your concentration to avoid death. The controls are responsive. Unlike Dark Souls, you can actually know if a weapon is going to hit you or not. In addition, your timed attacks will be much easier to hit. If you take the hard path in the game, a lot of caution is required as you can't just run in there slicing every monster you see. After all, they'll be coming at you from every different direction. The only thing I want to be implemented is the opportunity to be matched up with random people instead of only inviting people from your friends list. It really helps considering I don't have any friends lol.

Hero Academy is a great idea, and was really fun at first. I played a solid 10 hours on release and had a pretty good time battling with my friends.
Even if you aren't playing with your friends, the internet multiplayer option allows for quick and seamless matchmaking, meaning you can play as and when you want.
However, a few specificities of the game kind of ruin it. By default, the opening "move allowance" is set to be unfair against the person who creates the game, meaning that very very option (unless manually de-selected) your opponent (or you) will have a +3 or -3 move advantage, which very much affects the late stages of the game when every move counts.
This, for me, tilted the tables. I no longer felt I was playing a game, I felt I was inadvertantly cheating. Since then, I haven't played anymore.
A good game, but tweaking required for it to be fair. But, if you tweak your settings, you need to rely on your opponent doing so as well (which, by the way, they wont).

What Duke Nukem 3D and Shadow Warrior were to action and kung-fu movies, Blood is to slasher, horror films. Like the two games mentioned, Blood is an FPS game that uses the Build engine. What makes it different from the other two is the dark atmosphere, the enemies that range from gun-toting cultist and axe wielding zombies to hell hounds and stone gargoyles. The weapon variety of Blood is greatly varied, ranging from a flare gun and dynamite that can either burn or blow up a cultist to a tesla gun that can zap the life out of a hell hound. Gameplay in Blood is the same as Duke Nukem 3D and Shadow Warrior but it's also challenging, as some enemies can take a lot of punishment such as the mother spiders and the stone gargoyles and even some of the more mundane or basic foes such as cultist can put a dent in your health if your aren't careful.
If you're looking to buy a game that is dark, fun, and from an older time (that had good FPS games), Blood is one that should be given a chance.

Highly recomend to anyone looking for a really good story, intense violence and a hardcore look at racism in the south during the height of the civil rights era.  The games low ratings are mainly for the bugs present in the game and getting blown away by GTA V's free roam and diversity in every mission and side quest.  Luckily, for me, I did not play until well after release so my playthrogh went 99.5% bug free and the bugs that did occur did not break the game for me.
One word of caution though, the game is PC demanding.  After 4+ consecutive hours you do see the signs of overheating with voices getting out of lip synch, splattering textures and so on.  Another let down would be that they must have not talked to the right people about some of the popular music hits of the day.  Although the game has plenty of great music, you have no Beetles or other very recognizable gems of the day.
That story though.  Wow.  You get your moneys worth.  35+ hours of great gameplay that is never ending action, twists, turns and a whole lot of backstabbing.  With high replay value thanks to DLC's and how you can set up who oversees your rackets and crime syndicates, you are not wasting your money on this game one bit.
Even though it totally gets it's but kicked by GTA V in the diversity environment, the story and setting destroys GTA almost equally.  And seeing how they almost immediatly came down on their price tag while being the newer game, I have to give my review based on what the games price tag was at the time of purchase.
