Easily one of the best rhythm games to come out EVER. CoTND is a procedurally generated dungeon crawler with the difficulty and addictiveness of Binding of Isaac, with, imo, a killer soundtrack. This is probably because the music was made by the same guy but, I digress.
And if for some reason you hate the music (or you get sick of dying and hearing the same bloody song from level 1 over and over again like I do (inb4 'git good')) you can substitute the level songs with your own music.
You play at Cadence, one of several musically-named individuals who must make their way through the titular Crypt for their each individual reasons, which is fun but the true awesomeness lies in the music-related combat and sweet pixel art visuals. That being said the game is hard. It's really hard. The good news is with a few proper upgrades you can become veritably unstoppable in any of the worlds. The learning curve drops into a cliff about the time you meet the Red Dragon, who can take you out with a single well-timed fire breath from across the map, and he'll show up every now and again in Zone 1.
Easy to learn and hard to master are how I would describe this game, and would definitely recommend it unless you're known to break things if you get easily frustrated. Mice and keyboards are expensive.

An amalgamation of other MOBA type games with a few slight improvements but the same problems. It is yet another unfinished, early access, free to play game full of uneccessary microtransactions and meaningless cosmetic items that will probably be in beta for another 6-12 months at least. Simply put, it combines elements from Overwatch, Team Fortress, Heroes of the Storm, League of Legends, and Dota 2, so if you don't like any of those games, then you won't like this either. Yes, you can customize champions using a card system to accentuate different abilities, increase health or clip size, lower cooldowns, raise durations, but it only does so much. You earn money during the match to purchase additional passive boosts, many of which are worthless. You get a mount so you get back into the action more quickly, which is a neat idea. The game has decent graphics and performance, it is polished, and there isn't much lag. But aside from a few minor gameplay tweaks, this game has nothing we haven't seen already.
The issues I have with the game mainly come down to the champions and the community. One of the first things you notice is that almost every champion is a blatant rip off of someone from Overwatch. Viktor is Soldier 76,  Evie is Mei, Lex is Reaper, Androxus is McCree, Maeve is Genji, Barik is Torbjorn, Drogoz is Pharah, Ruckus is D. Va, Fernando is Reinhardt, etc. Yes, there are slight differences in their abilities and movements, but it's easy to figure out who each champion is inspired by. Just like in the games I mentioned, in their effort to make the champions unique, the developers have made them completely unbalanced. I do give them credit for including a feedback system that let's you specify which champions you think need a nerf or buff. In general, the champions have high damage, low health, and no accuracy. There is no skill, you just keep firing from the hip and hope you hit someone. The support heroes can't heal enough to make a difference, while the front liners have way too much shielding. You cannot aim down the sites, unless you pick Viktor. That's one of many examples of balance issues: being the only champion who can aim down the sites gives him an unfair advantage, plus his ultimate ability is way too strong. In fact, all the damage dealers, and even some of the front liners and flankers, have ultimate abilities that are overpowered. Skye's ultimate is an instant kill and has way too much range, easily getting a team kill and play of the game.
Matchmaking is non existent. You are repeatedly teamed up with people who clearly do not understand their role, while facing off against opponents of much higher skill level. Supports don't heal, flankers don't flank, and when you play a front liner, you get scolded for being on the front line. At the character select screen, you'll often see 3-4 people all choosing damage heroes, and you'll often have matches with no support or front liner. Just like the other games I mentioned, everyone wants to shell out the most damage and get the most kills, often forsaking the team and objective in the process. You find yourself being the only person on the objective, getting ambushed by the entire enemy team, only to have your teammates swear at you. No one uses chat to formulate strategy, they just use it to insult each other. I haven't experienced any disconnections mid game, but I've had many instances of high queue times and failed connection attempts. No lag for the most part, but issues with hit detection. There are times when you unload a whole clip without hitting someone only to get one shotted, and when you watch the killcam, their bullets didn't even hit you. (it's not as bad as Call of Duty, but still annoying.)
I hate Overwatch, played only a few matches of DOTA and LoL, and recently quit HotS after playing about 1,000 matches, I only tried this game because it was free, and while it is a much better game than Overwatch, it still got boring quickly.
My advice to anyone thinking about getting into this game or any of the others I mentioned: Don't. The time investment is not worth the frustration.

This game is extremely fun and offers depth that hearthstone lacks. Upon first playing it, there are obvious imitations of heartstone present at face value. But after playing it for a couple of hours, you soon notice how much better SC is.
Pros:
Its sci-fi based
It offers more advanced card techniques like area attacking
Its less money-greedy (you can actually get legendary cards without spending a dime)
Board placement is more relevant than in HS
The ranking system is much better, once you reach a certain rank, you cant drop below it and there doesnt seem to be as frequent of resets atm
Much more freedom when creating a deck. The minimum is 25, the max is 40
Cons
Graphics and UI could be smoothened out
It still feels like HS
Offers less game modes and events than HS (but to be fair its just in  beta)
*****************EDITED 03/06/2017***********************
Here's an update a year later and no longer in beta. Played beta for 80 hours, and in the past weeks played another 80 hours.
Pros:
Its still sci-fi based
It still offers more advanced card techniques like area attacking
Its still less money-greedy (you can actually get legendary cards without spending a dime)
Board placement is still more relevant than in HS
The ranking system isn't actually any different from hearthstone. (I use HS to compare because this is what most people know). The rewards are ALOT more generous however.
There is still much more freedom when creating a deck. The minimum is 25, the max is 40 cards. Your health is the amount of cards you have so a 25 deck will keep your cards concise but you have 15 less hp than a 40 card deck and run the risk of drawing out your cards if you face a later game opponent.
Cons
Graphics and UI could be smoothened out
The game no longer feels like hearthstone at all and they have a new mode called raid mode which is basically the arena in hearthstone, but better. There is a map and you can choose your paths you take and you spots you land on can actually yield bonus rewards. You basically loot or plunder each planet you capture (defeat another player) I've won 12 games once in this mode and came out with a ton of rewards.
There is also a story mode as well now and on top of the rewards being generous, there is also cutscenes to tell the story of all this stuff. (im not a story person so dont ask what the hell its even about)
Loot crates - These are basically bonus rewards on top of everything else they are giving away for free which gives you a bunch of nice rewards and its totally free. You can buy with money of course or you can wait from 4 hrs to 24 hrs depending on your crates level. They had no reason to give players this for free but the fact that they did just shows that they want to make a game people will like.
Hero gear - I dont find this too interesting but you can dress up your commander so that ppl using the same deck have unique avatars. It doesnt provide in game bonus its just customization but its not really in depth as there are only 3 possible item designs per body part. So in the end everyone is basically the same looking but maybe a slight color difference on your helmet. It's better than nothing I guess and given more options could become cooler.
Daily rewards - Theres a calendar for each month and logging in will net greater rewards until the end of the month. Miss a day and you basically miss out on the best stuff at the end of the month.
Modules - When these were first released, I didnt really like them I thought they over complicated things. But now I love them they make things so interesting. Its basically like the hero power in hearthstone, but imagine like 30 different powers to choose from and you can choose up to 3! They are just as important to a deck as any card although ive won games without using them. But to get the perfectly synced deck, youre going to have to use these. They are also found in booster packs though so to get the rare ones youre gonna have to farm or use dust to buy them.
I think that covered all the additions since my beta testing. Overall I love this game and if you like card games and want to support a company that actually puts thought into their game, try this one out.

This is a great new CCG and plays like HS but is sci-fi, runs on Steam and overall runs very smooth for being in Beta. The balance among the races is really good as I have been able to win with each one several times. The developer seems to listen and take in community suggestions during the beta/early access and has put out some updates and another one is right around the corner.  Also the prizes and giveaways are generous, more than other games I have played in recent memory which is nice.
Not sure why people downvote the game because it is like Blizzard HS CCG. They are all CCG online games and there is only so much variety, but this one is worth your time if you are sick of HS, like sci-fi or are new to CCG and want to get in and try from the ground up before 100,000 people are playing (which I can only hope for).
Oh and all cards you gain during beta/early access are yours, the game is not being wiped according to developers upon official release 1.0, whenever that will be.
A few things to note for someone just starting off:
1)  there is no help within the game beyond the quick tutorial. (It is planned supposedly but not impletmented yet).  You will feel lost at times, but after about 10 hours and many non-ranked games you get a feel for things fairly quick.  If you have played other CCGs online this curve will be a bit less steep for you.
2)  there are not 100,000 players so at this time during early access you do play a lot of high end players and can/may get frustrated when you start off. I know I did at first and wanted to pitch my screen across the desk after 3 rounds in a row vs top 5 opponent. BUT it is also a great time to learn and debug the game,and once I came to terms with that I have been progressing more and seeing the great CCG that it is.
3)  Raids are great as it is a random pick of 30 cards.  But remember you will not have the experience and knowledge of combos and playstyles under your belt so you will be destroyed 90% of the time until you learn.  Do not waste your credits on Raids until you have a lot of spare credits lying around. Once I stopped raiding and started using the earned credits for packs my non-raid decks got better, i started enjoying the game more, and then I was able to throw in a raid now and again and I win 1 or 2 raid games out of 5 games where I used to lose 3 straight and raid was over. But to each their own, odds are you are better than I am at this game. :)
4)  There is a new players guide up on Steam which wasn't there when I started. Read it. WIll help with the knowledge base and allow you to build a playable deck without all the top cards (which aren't needed as much as I thought).

As a fan of OMD! and OMD!2, I was worried about this installment being f2p and focused on pvp. I was very disappointed with the early beta as it was clear OMDU was nothing but tpp MOBA.
Luckily the devs have realised their mistake and now the game plays mostly like classic OMD!. While pvp isn't gone completely, it's only one of a few modes with all others being pve.
Graphics, sound, controls feel very familiar, so it's quite easy to jump in and play. There are some changes like guardians, a variety of heroes but the essence, meaning building traps, is the same.
The interface might be a bit overwhelming at the beginning with multiple tabs, modes, upgrades, parts, stores etc, but everything becomes clear with time. However I'd like to see some improvements in this matter. Perhaps certain tabs should be disabled and would be unlocked as players progress through tutorial or the first few maps?
Another thing I don't really like is that there are two separate applications with separate options and configuration. One is sort of a command centre where you select the next level, your loadout, hero, make purchases etc., and the other which is the game itself. It doesn't feel or look right.
My playtime at the moment is 76h and so far I haven't reached a point where I'm unable to progress unless I spend some money. I can feel the game becoming more and more difficult, but still manageable and it's a good thing because I enjoy challenge.
Overall it's a great game and if you liked OMD! and OMD!2, you should enjoy it as well.

I'm not going to knock this game because it's a Hearthstone clone.  It plays exactly like hearthstone, but with a sci-fi theme, and frankly, that doesn't have to be a bad thing.
I'm knocking this game for being...well..stupid.  Or broken, I can't tell which.
My main issues are:
1) I can't unlock any factions.  Game says "defeat these leaders in any game mode to unlock the faction".  Ok, super.  Problem is that you can't create any custom games to choose a leader you want to challenge.  Your opponents are completely random when playing the AI and you never get a faction that you weren't given by default when you started.
You also can't purchase any faction unlocks or leaders with the in-game currency that you earn from winning or doing quests/dailies.
2) You can't buy anything other than booster packs, currently.  The store hints at all these things to unlock with the money you receive, but you can't actually buy anything.
3) It's about as rich in story as a Kardashian biography.  There's just a bunch of random factions with short blurbs about each leader, nothing to really tie them together, certainly no campaigns available to starting players- at least none that I can unlock....
The artwork is good, the UI is simple, if not better than HearthStone, but the menus and mouseovers could use some work.  The animations and background are pretty good as well.
I'll change my rating if things change, but currently, can't recommend, pretty stale experience gameplay wise and pretty frustrating to not be able to explore the game fully.
Edit** I'll now bump this up to a 5/10 and recommend the game by the slimmest of margins.  I suddenly got to play some different commanders to play against (squeaky wheel?? lol) so perhaps my RNG in drawing a different commander was just horri-bad, but it still doesn't change the fact that you can't choose who you want to play and the store is still busted.

General features (can be viewed as pros):
-Race customization is fairly detailed
-Ship designer is good, even better because you can use pre-existing models and modify them to your own tastes
-Certain resources are linked to certain celestial bodies eg antimatter surround black holes, elerium in nebulae, etc. So a savvy player, upon seeing a nebula knows to explore it fully incase there is elerium and that a black hole is likely to have some antimatter surrounding it.
-powerful resources like antimatter are more limited, but using them is non-destructive so there wont be buyers remorse, ie you'll get the resource back if you destroy the building/ship that uses it. This also allows you to use resources early in buildings tech, and then recycle it when a better option arrives, meaning that a player who can manage his resources well will do better than one who just holds onto resources until a "top tier" usage for them is unlocked.
-massive maps are possible, so with the right settings it doesnt feel like a "small" galaxy or that you're running out of space (until late game)
-starbases used intelligently can give an edge at all points in the game, especially economic starbases. eg rather than waste a building slot on your planet to raise approval, just get the approval upgrade on the starbase linked to the planet.
-able to finely control research/economy output/dedication on planets individually, but also with the "govern" tab you can do this en mass, saving time. Same applys for upgrading ships, etc.
-every planet has an event, which some may find annoying, but I think is good, allows you do add a slight layer of uniqueness to each planet as well as develop your ideology.
-its actually more beneficial long terms to dabble in all ideologies to some extent, as long as your primary ideology has most points you wont have an ideological shift. This means you dont have to do the unrealistic option (as in some games with ideologies/religions) and devote 100% to an ideology. This also means, if desired, you can play on the basis of the moral choices involved for events/planets and still do OK in terms of ideological benefit (as opposed to number crunching the statistical/numerical benefits for each choice planet, etc)
Cons
- diplomacy at first seems well developed, but that's only for early game. Late game diplomacy is at best, shallow, at worst, buggy. "Benevolent" ideologies seem to hate pragmatic ideologies as much as "malevolent" ideologies, which is silly and means that as a pragmatist, you need to kill anyone else who isn't a pragmatist and can only really form alliances with other pragmatists. This makes a diplomacy victory in a large game close to impossible without a decent military (because you need to kill anyone who refuses to ally with you), which means its always going to be predominantly a conquest based game.
--continuing on for diplomacy: enemies will gladly colonise planets within starsystems you have partially colonized and there's no warning to tell them to♥♥♥♥♥♥off (as in games like CIV 5), and the same for resources. Early game is basically en-mass resource grab if you dont want to be screwed over mid/late game.
-pirates/barbarians in 4X games are normally some kind of great equalizer early game to prevent a military/expansion snowball (eg sins of a solar empire, civ, etc), but in this game they're just annoying and dont do much besides kill the occasional scout. also, AI dont appear to be bothered by pirates, so its just a player handicap.
-once you start going balls to the walls crazy large military, the game will start glitching out your "military power" parameter, which means for the purposes of diplomacy, one turn later everyone will think you're the weakest, declare war/♥♥♥♥ with you even though you could wipe them out. this also contributes to the impossiblity of a diplomacy victory (without killing loads of people)
-terraforming in the incorrect order can cost you between 1-3 tiles per planet, which is a fair amount. eg if you use a higher grade terraformer on a "easy" tile, you wont be able to terraform the "harder" tiles, as late game you can terraform as many "easy" tiles as you like, meaning its better long term to hold off on terraforming until you've researched it fully as it isnt always clear which tiles are "easy" or "hard".
-money is weak, it can take anywhere between 5-15 turns to be able to afford to rush construction (pretty much the only use of money, besides upgrading your military ships) whereas focusing on manufacturing allows you to build anything in 1-3 turns. Basically as long as you break even with your economy, you can just focus on manufacturing and research. Its actually usually better to just decommission old ships and build news ones rather than upgrade them (which will make you bankrupt quick if you have a large army)
---In other words with the diplomacy + economy balancing, there is no viable economy based strategy or peaceful based strategy. No matter what, you will always need the strongest military regardless of your intended method of victory (unlike some other 4X games, where you could have an adequate military and with good diplomacy/economy still obtain most victory types you desire). And basically to get the strongest military you need to focus on research and manufacturing.
- united galaxies is but a shallow addition to the game, furthermore, if someone ever defies (which is almost always), they are permanently booted, which can lead to the ridiculous situation of having a united galaxy meeting of 2 members, while the other 6-10 races are "defiant" (yet have not formed another united galaxies).
meh features:
-culture. you must have decent culture to stop other races culture from "flipping" your planets, it also creates territorial space and (I think) it allows your ships to fly further into enemy space. problem is that if your culture is too strong it flips the planets of other races, including that of your allies. this makes your allies weaker and it entirely possible for them to be wiped off the map (further adding to the difficulty of a diplomacy victory). It also may land you a bunch of crap planets that you dont want to deal with. Fortunately you can give the♥♥♥♥♥♥planets to the minor races (who are immune to culture flipping)
note: most of these issues dont apply to multiplayer games, this is predominantly a critique of single player. although culture flipping feature will suck when playing co-op with friends.

The fourth game in the lego star wars series, Lego star wars 3 is a special one since it's about the Clone Wars cartoon instead of the movies. I wish this game was made a little bit later but not too late since some of the cooler episodes were not out yet when the game was made, but i also like that they still have grunts and moans instead of voice acting.
what is new in this game?
You choose what missions you want to start with instead of going on a linear path. you play episode to episode. The best part about it is that it's in actual chronological order! yes you heard that. the game actually follows the story in chronological order unlike the show which released the episodes in a random order!
There are more features such as gold bricks that have to be destroyed with rapid fire weapons, throwable lightsabers, combo moves, quick time events, and more. i'll talk about the biggest ones next.
There is now a bigger hub ship with tons of rooms to unlock and secrets to be discovered. Once you open up the hangar you can actually take a ship and fly to the seperatist ship and change hubs to the evil side where you can buy separatist characters and ships AND even play sith side missions!
The other big mission features are ground battles where the game throws you into an empty and big level with areas to build bases and turrets. You attack and take over other bases by making troop barracks sort of like a RTS but you get to battle too.
There are now more customizable characters than the usual 2 we saw in lego star wars 2 and complete saga.
The music is taken from the episodes the missions take place in so no more do we have repeated tracks from the movies in every single enemy encounter, every episode has different music. Like i mentioned before the game is based on the show , but it's based on the first seasons. The clones are still in phase 2 so there are no episode 3 ships or clone troopers like we see later in the show.
OVERALL is this game better than 2? in features and gameplay yes! but for those people who never bothered to watch The clone wars cartoon they might not like the setting. the humor is still here! the cutscenes are longer then before and    even a little bit better. the characters now have more face expersions which give them more personality.
another thing that will make you enjoy the game is the lack of the pointless voice acting that started with lego batman 2. The silence of the characters make it funnier and their own style. Graphics are more shiny than before and the characters more detailed. GET THIS GAME IF YOU ARE A FAN.!! my rating would be a 9/10

An amalgamation of other MOBA type games with a few slight improvements but the same problems. It is yet another unfinished, early access, free to play game full of uneccessary microtransactions and meaningless cosmetic items that will probably be in beta for another 6-12 months at least. Simply put, it combines elements from Overwatch, Team Fortress, Heroes of the Storm, League of Legends, and Dota 2, so if you don't like any of those games, then you won't like this either. Yes, you can customize champions using a card system to accentuate different abilities, increase health or clip size, lower cooldowns, raise durations, but it only does so much. You earn money during the match to purchase additional passive boosts, many of which are worthless. You get a mount so you get back into the action more quickly, which is a neat idea. The game has decent graphics and performance, it is polished, and there isn't much lag. But aside from a few minor gameplay tweaks, this game has nothing we haven't seen already.
The issues I have with the game mainly come down to the champions and the community. One of the first things you notice is that almost every champion is a blatant rip off of someone from Overwatch. Viktor is Soldier 76,  Evie is Mei, Lex is Reaper, Androxus is McCree, Maeve is Genji, Barik is Torbjorn, Drogoz is Pharah, Ruckus is D. Va, Fernando is Reinhardt, etc. Yes, there are slight differences in their abilities and movements, but it's easy to figure out who each champion is inspired by. Just like in the games I mentioned, in their effort to make the champions unique, the developers have made them completely unbalanced. I do give them credit for including a feedback system that let's you specify which champions you think need a nerf or buff. In general, the champions have high damage, low health, and no accuracy. There is no skill, you just keep firing from the hip and hope you hit someone. The support heroes can't heal enough to make a difference, while the front liners have way too much shielding. You cannot aim down the sites, unless you pick Viktor. That's one of many examples of balance issues: being the only champion who can aim down the sites gives him an unfair advantage, plus his ultimate ability is way too strong. In fact, all the damage dealers, and even some of the front liners and flankers, have ultimate abilities that are overpowered. Skye's ultimate is an instant kill and has way too much range, easily getting a team kill and play of the game.
Matchmaking is non existent. You are repeatedly teamed up with people who clearly do not understand their role, while facing off against opponents of much higher skill level. Supports don't heal, flankers don't flank, and when you play a front liner, you get scolded for being on the front line. At the character select screen, you'll often see 3-4 people all choosing damage heroes, and you'll often have matches with no support or front liner. Just like the other games I mentioned, everyone wants to shell out the most damage and get the most kills, often forsaking the team and objective in the process. You find yourself being the only person on the objective, getting ambushed by the entire enemy team, only to have your teammates swear at you. No one uses chat to formulate strategy, they just use it to insult each other. I haven't experienced any disconnections mid game, but I've had many instances of high queue times and failed connection attempts. No lag for the most part, but issues with hit detection. There are times when you unload a whole clip without hitting someone only to get one shotted, and when you watch the killcam, their bullets didn't even hit you. (it's not as bad as Call of Duty, but still annoying.)
I hate Overwatch, played only a few matches of DOTA and LoL, and recently quit HotS after playing about 1,000 matches, I only tried this game because it was free, and while it is a much better game than Overwatch, it still got boring quickly.
My advice to anyone thinking about getting into this game or any of the others I mentioned: Don't. The time investment is not worth the frustration.

The most important thing you should know about LiEat is that IT'S NOT AN RPG.
LiEat is a visual novel stuffed in the RPG format.
Combat, gear, HP and SP are purely an accessory to telling a story.
They're trivial and pose no difficulty.
This is how you'll spend 95% of your time in the game:
-reading through NPC dialogue;
-walking from place A to place B to talk to an NPC, or go pick up an item;
-walking aimlessly to find place B that will progress the story because no one hinted at what or where it is.
Combat is just padding between the actions above. You'd have to make an effort to die, and you can get out of every encounter by keeping A pressed to basically auto-attack.
I don't have a problem with story driven games. The problem is when they're advertised as something they're not.
I think this type of doujin game isn't simply cut for the western market, or at least not for a storefront like Steam... But apparently the other reviews think otherwise.
Anyway, if you can get past the above, the story is run-of-the-mill cute anime; it's nothing special, but it works. It feels like watching one of those random 11-episode anime that you find passable as you're watching them, only to forget them them in a couple of weeks after you're done watching the last episode and being mildly dissatisfied.
The Steam release is made up of 3 shorter games (LiEat 1 to 3) which tell three different stories about the two main characters visiting three different locations and working on as many mysteries/crimes. These all consist in small locations where you run around completing fetch quests, with all the triggers (item hidden in a bookshelf, picture found in a book, note in the trash can...) that don't activate until you've hit a certain story flag, so get ready to search all the trash cans in the area each time you progress with the story.
In short, unless you're a very bored very game-hungry anime fan, avoid this game as it's not worth the time needed to drag yourself through it.

It's rare for me to complete single player games. Normally I loose interest before I get to the end. Not with Trapped Dead. I played it through to the end and loved all of it.
The story isn't great (it's no Walking Dead), but it's just good enough to create a relaxing b-movie feel (which is almost tradition for zombie movies!).
The engine and the controls are a bit... quirky, at times, but for some reason those quirks created character rather than annoyance. It's like that cute lovable dog that's the runt of the litter.
The game mechanics aren't at all innovative. It's got your classic RPG features that you would expect. I felt that this game has just the right amount of complexity that I felt challenged, but not so much complexity that I felt like playing it required lots of effort. I could get home from work and put some casual hours into it with what was left of my brain and still feel a strong sense of reward for my in-game accomplishments.
The game is well balanced. It's consistent: once you understand how to play it, you can enjoy it all without feeling stuck or getting confused.
If you like RPGs and zombie movies and if you can drop your standards below the likes of Baldur's Gate and XCOM, then you'll probably enjoy this.

I started playing this and Hearthstone at the same time, so I'm late to Digital CCG, but I have played MTG off and on for 15+ years, so the concept is hardly new.  After playing both Hearthstone and Star Crusade, I prefer Star Crusade.  I find there more diversity on how the board is controlled, within the factions play styles, and multi-turn synergy/combos.  It can be easy to download, play a few hands, and dismiss as "Hearthstone in SPACE" (Warcraft the Gathering?), but if you stick with it you will quickly see how it defines itself differently.  The basic cards you get are decently strong and I have had success with them while earning packs, so you are not immediately at a huge disadvantage.  I hope they are some how able to maintain this, as it allowed me to get into the game quickly and not eye roll when my opponents are playing the same legendary cards match after match.
Other than the game itself, the UI is good.  Some of the card art is great, while some is laughable. Rythm-based roguelike dungeon crawler, where you have to press buttons to the beat of the music to move each turn.
Putting aside the rythm gimmick, the game plays like a simple grid-based dungeon crawler. As you slay monsters and descend through the crypt, you find a variety of equipable items that upgrade your character. Enemy attacks come in predictable patterns which can be dodged, and your attacks likewise hit with different patterns depending on what weapon you use. The tactics aren't complicated, but it's easy to slip up when you're tasked with making several moves per second. The combination of speed, timing, and strategy is unique and feels very satisfying once you get the hang of it.
The story, told through cutscenes, is unremarkable but not bad. Furthermore, the voice acting and pixel art are good, and the music is stellar. The game's focus is on its mechanics, but it manages to cobble together a compelling atmosphere as well.
Playing each of the game's four zones one by one is relatively easy and allows you to buy upgrades between runs, but the marathon "all zones mode" is much more challenging. There are also several playable characters, each with their own mechanics, as well as local co-op multiplayer.
A hugely successful experiment - lots of fun.

Checked out this game because, honestly, Sci-Fi and Card Game is generally up my alley. Didn't take long to realize it's a Sci-Fi painting of Hearthstone of course, as many reviews have pointed out. But at first it didn't bother me. Honestly I never cared for the style of Warcraft myself so I thought I'd give it an honest try.
The problems though mostly relate to difficulty curve. Hearthstone, as much as I might not personally care for it, at least has a decent chance of making matches that you feel like you at least had a chance at it. Yes I get curb stomped sometimes, but I never felt completely impotent and outmatched in these horrible, one sided squashes.
But that's what Star Crusade is at its heart. Once I got out of the tutorial game, I never faced a single match where I was anything but hopelessly outclassed. Even when I tried the Raid Mode, figuring that as a Draft Mode we'd all be on equal footing Deck Wise with the challenges out there, I got utterly destroyed in 3 straight rounds against the first "Easy" mission of the Raid. No contest, barely got any offense in and hardly could have a card in play for a full turn, and those cases only if I got the first card drop.
You might read this, think it just means I suck, which could be fair. But it's not like I'm a Card Game newb either, done plenty of Draft Nights for Magic, etc. I get the basic theories of the game, the basic probabilities and mechanics. The only thing I can guess is involved in this utter crushing is two factors...
One is a lack of good match making/balancing formulas for the game. A major problem, the sort of thing that can ruin your night as much as stepping into your first Ladder Qualifier games in StarCraft II only to find yourself getting mopped up by a Diamond Leaguer 5 times in a row. Possible that it could be fixed but until it does, it'll just be bad times.
But the Raid Mode revealed a second issue perhaps at hand, as I got to play against the same deck and AI three times in a row. They stack the enemy's deck. Legitimately every single game started with the exact same 7 first turn drops for the enemy. Considering you start with 4 cards in a 40 card deck the chance that you could even have the same turn one drop (2 Cards duped in a deck max) is astronomical. Suggests a huge screw job with the enemy Bots and such.
For my time, I rather not face what is effectively someone so blatantly cheating and being so heavily outmatched that if I were playing at the Tabletop with them I'd reach over and slap them.

I think this game gets more abuse than it deserves and I think herein lays great potential for a new take on zombie games.  Not that I'm recommending this game on its potential alone.
Where there can be filler sections, there are a good smattering of genuinely exciting sections where you have to tactically micromanage your team's position, weaponry and targets to escape the hordes that are rolling inexorably over your position.  Cramped indoors or built up urban areas add to this excitement, where every move is key.  I found the game's difficulty relatively on the low side though (no difficulty settings either), and was never short of ammunition but the game is swift to punish carelessness as your guys can become zombie chow in 2 seconds if left unattended next to a hungry undead.
The story plays homage to all the zombie cliches in a suitably brief (only about 8 or so hours of gameplay so it doesn't outstay it's welcome) tour of all the standard zombie invasion locations.  There are rough bits granted, and it could be buggy at times.  I had at least one crash to desktop, and sometimes injured zombies would suddenly stand up many metres from where you had smashed/blasted them to.  Also there are some truly bizarre choices at times (the end credits ends on a box of cereal) and the ending was a bit of a flop, leaving me with a bit of an anticlimx as the only thing resembling a boss fight coming on the penultimate level.
I will allow there are better zombie games out there.  Though if you love all things zombies and tire of the standard run and gun zombie kill-a-thon then this could be the game for you.  Definitely pick it up on sale.

A nice compelation of the three LiEat games. I've always loved Miwashibas games, and while LiEat is actually my least favorite of their works, it's still a nice series in it's own ways. Miwashibas art is great, and other then 1bitheart's sprites, it feels the most polished in the pure amount of CG's and Movies that are in the game. Miwashiba has also always had great character designs in general, and with how the main characters change in appearance (Efinas papa especially) it's fun seeing how they evolve.
The story can be enjoyable depending on your preference. For the most part it feels like episodical games ala shonen anime, but the first game is somewhat connected to it's prologue novel, and the last game is very character centric over the main characters past. I do feel like there should have been more fleshing out on the characters and story, and the battle system honestly isn't neccessary. I think Miwashiba realized that fault, since their later game doesn't include a battle system at all, instead opting for Dangan Ronpa/Ace Attorney style gameplay.  All in all, LiEat has it's faults, but it is genuinly a fun and beautiful game to play, and I also reccomend playing miwashibas other games, Alice_Mare and 1bitheart if you find yourself enjoying miwashibas storytelling, characters, and art.

Good things:
1) Level design is really good - and in a game where the enemy variety is not that great levels are very important.

Evil, bad things:

A series of short, cute mystery RPGs. The graphics style took a bit to get used to, but after a while it grew on me. It's a unique art style from what I know, and it's actually kind of cute. The music is pretty good, too, and the 3 games are each like episodic parts of the universe that serve as character development. That being said, I still recommend playing them in order so as to understand the overarcing plot better. As for the combat and gameplay, it's rather simple, with you facing off against lies (there's no consequence really if you mislabel truths and lies) and using pretty much the same strategy for each boss. The story is good, though it's pretty linear, which is fine. There are, of course, bad and good endings, so I guess it's not 100% linear in that manner.
Tldr; if you want a short mystery story with a cute art style, some combat, and good music, here's a good one right here.

What you get when buying this game is a whole bunch of Soviet Cold War era vehicles, rough terrain, logs....and mud. Most of the game centers around you and your driving skills, as well as how well you know and can handle your chosen vehicle. Driving in this game is pretty straightforward. WASD for basic movements, Q and E for differential and AWD/RWD/FWD modes, spacebar for parking brakes. But the challenge lies in actually tackling the terrain. A simple mud pit, let alone a river, can ruin your vehicle.
Driving the vehicles is satisfying, really. There's something gratifying about driving huge 8-wheeled trucks into mud pools. The physics system is pretty cool though. Seeing your truck displace water, make tracks in the mud and seeing the suspension at work tackling rocks and rough slopes is satisfying. Maybe its just a childhood fantasy made reality really. It's fun. One gripe I have about this game is the camera angles. It's pretty good for panning all around the vehicle to check your surroundings, but there's no first person cockpit view. The roof view doesn't count though. Just a small gripe, though.
Gameplay wise revolves mainly around delivering logs from one point to another point. Lots of ground to cover between you and your objective, and anything can go wrong. Main challenge here lies in the terrain, as said before, though there's nothing else to it. Multiplayer is something that frankly I haven't touched as there's no servers ATM.
If you like big trucks, mud and rough terrain, get this one. One thing to note is that the development of this game seems to be dead from what I heard, so get it on sale.

Okay, class. This review is now in session. Now...let's analyze this game to see where it went wrong...starting with the description...sentence by sentence.
"Do not underestimate the apparent simplicity of OR because it will amaze you." True, this game is of a simple design. So simple in fact that
comes off as primitive. Keeping that in mind, you will not be amazed....though activating protective barriers do restore 1 HP, so...that's something.
"In the game there will be pitfalls of every kind!" I made my way into world 6 (really, level 6). Now, there aren't many pitfalls in this game. Mostly just barriers, light balls to chase you, and walls that kill you instantly. No spikes, no pits....wait....pits....aren't those...."Pitfalls"?
"The 3D graphics allows you to see the light from above." That's humorous, TECHNICALLY I guess you could call this a 3D game with the walls and corners, but with how this game is portrayed, it may as well be a 2D game...where you DON'T need 3D graphics to see lights from above. Now...what defines something as 3D? If you say "the usage of the X, Y, and Z axis", then you're correct and get a cookie!
"This opens up a world of possible combinations." But none you haven't seen before. Your color matches a barrier and you're able to pass through it without being harmed.
"With gameplay based around light, OR is a simplified Puzzle/Arcade game." Gameplay based around light? Yes. You play as a light source trying to make it to the big ball of white light as the matching white light polarity. Yes, it is simplified (as stated earlier), but calling this game "arcade" is a stretch. There is a level ("world") selector, but no matter how far you get, you'll find that it's quite unresponsive. The level selector may as well not exist. And yes, pressing ESC means you'll have to play all over again...starting at the very...first...tutorial. In addition, gameplay only seems to run smoothly so long as you're moving. When you're sitting still, though, it slows to a crawl...shouldn't it normally be the other way around due to rendering?
"Play through 10 worlds with progressive difficulty, let the light guide you!" Ahem....please turn your attention to Exhibit A...Does it look like 10 levels to you? Maybe in Base 15... And I'm fairly certain that YOU'RE guiding the light...
Description analysis complete. If you're feeling disappointed in this game or this developer, then that's understandable. I feel we've learned that a descriptive review really helps a game and, unfortunately, this game suffers from a description that betrays itself.
is priced at $1, but feels like a free flash game. Although it goes on sale for $0.50, don't spend any money on OR as an individual purchase. You may find it in a bundle...where it's usually best to buy games like this. But even then, I'm only glad that this game has trading cards. I appreciate that this developer tried to make a halfway decent game, but it severely suffers from the lack of polish.

Okay so I have about 22 hours under belt so I am going to weigh in here.  While I owned and played a good deal of GC1 and GC2 they were always so/so to me.  I enjoyed them and got my money out of them but they never really engaged me as much as I would like to have been able to say that they did.  GC3 so far is holding my fancy though pretty good.  It has some flaws, the AI like most 4X games sucks at diplomacy.  The biggest sell to me is the HUGE maps.  I like games that go into the 500-1000 turn range and this game has that in spades with the larger maps.
The game does suffer from some CTD (Crash To Desktop) from time to time but that is when I am on huge and larger maps, and it is somewhat expected with a new game.   The CTD haven't really hurt my progress as I save often but they could cause someone to be upset if they don't save enough.
One bad thing is that Stardock is clearly in the game for the long haul and has plans to release DLC and expansions regularly.  This is a plus and minus.  I like a steady stream of content but there are some things that I feel like were left out of the game just to be an easy sell later on like Spies and other races.   This isn't a huge deal though as I am a game collector and I don't mind decent DLC/expansions.  I spend a small fortune with games like Crusader Kings 2 and Europa Universalis IV so I am used to this sort of deal.  However if you want a full experience I would suggest waiting later and picking up the game in a few years (if you can wait that long) for a complete edition at a sale price.
But if you enjoy the genre and don't mind having to pay as you go for features to be added here and there the game is worth the money.

I'm a fan of the Galactic Civilizations series, however I feel this game steps backwards in a few areas. The shipyards, while a cool idea, can be annoying. If you don't have a fleet strong enough you can't defend your shipyard from aggression, so they made the shipyard overpowered in the early game which can be annoying if you have pirates right outside your doorstep. You also can't build starports on your home planet which is probably because you'd have a planet building two ships at once. But all you need to do is make it so that a planet with a starport can't build ships at shipyards. The fact that you can't build starports on planets is contradictory to the campaign where Earth built a massive armada at the height where planes fly without a shipyard. The last negative is the campaign. While this game's main draw is the singleplayer sandbox, the campaign deserves the same attention the gal civ 2 campaign got. There's three missions, 2 cutscenes (the first one being the best part of the campaign) and some nice dialogue. I beat the campaign in two days. I won't spoil the end, but trust me it's not worth it. Also it doesn't explain the rest of the story, which I was hoping for. I was also hoping Stardock would explain how the Iridium Corporation came to be in game. That way you wouldn't have to search for it on the website. But at the end of the day it's all about the money and I think Stardock is going to release a dlc and force it's customers to pay to complete the story. I was really hoping Stardock wouldn't stoop to that level. As for the rest of the game I think it's a fantastic game. I wished they still had those mega events from gal civ 2 because as far as I know there are none. Final Verdict is 7/10, mostly because the story was very disappointing and the shipyards oh god the shipyards. However I do recommend the game for 4x fans.

[Minor spoilers about end game gameplay].
I had been in the Crypt for almost 20 hours before I first encountered the Necrodancer.
I'd like to talk of that experience:
The identity of the Dead Ringer revealed, I felt a pang of confusion, only to hear him guide me, and then to realize I had to juggle two heroes terrified me. How many runs had I failed this far? And another boss after what already seemed like an impossible ordeal.
It only took me a few moments to realize the new mechanic I had to juggle in the last fight, and it was an amazing surprise which immediately filled the dancer floor with new energy.
I spent the first minute of the encounter with the Necrodancer keeping my heroes side by side, getting used to the beat. The easy beginning really affords those fighting Necrodancer for the first time the time they need to get ready.
And then, one by one I begin aligning my heroes, triggering bombs to the stage--not too difficult.
When the Necrodancer took to the dance floor, indeed was my heart beating at the  120bpm step, in sync with the Necrodancer himself.  I begrudgingly set aside my Obsidian Crossbow and equipped the Golden Lute, determined to do this right. At first, I ran from his reanimated fiends and explosive spells, trying to realign myself and regroup with my ally, but as soon as I understood his rhythm I slided in for a hit. The Necrodancer skips away only losing a single heart from my note, summoning more monsters between us.
Black Knights began to flank me on all sides and it's a challenge to keep them off with my ally's Flail. At one point I realize the Golden Lute can only sing its music if Cadence has a empty tile to move to, so being surrounded by shield bearing skeletons on two sides and a wall and ally covering the other two, I struggle to make any movements at all, all while rapidly losing health. For an instant I fear the worst, but in the next beat does my ally bash his Flail fowards, knocking back one skeleton--I immediately pounce on the next beat, allowing my Lute to sound the minions to dust.
The fight continues with me piercing again and again with my Lute, bringing the Necrodancer to a third of his health, while monsters continue to scratch my ally and I. In the fight I've lost four of my nine hearts, leaving both my ally and I at one and a half hearts left, and as I continue to hit the Necrodancer do increasingly powerful monsters seem to appear.
Eventually, there are too many skeletons in erratic formations I can't easily line up to attack, their pursuit herding me to one side of the dance floor where an Ogre has just joined. I've died many times to Ogres in the fourth zone, but I know the brute, slow, can be defeated if I merely kite around it. However, I worry that in the process, the new ally by my side would then get smashed in the ensuing blow. I move in, hitting him again and again as I circle to his back.
It was at that time, checking the hearts of my ally and I, going over the directional combinations to use bombs, switching to my holstered weapon or beating my war drum, as well as predicting the path of the many dancers of the Necrodancer did I make my fatal error. My attention split, I panic and move one tile away from the Ogre, immediately attracting his singularly directed club.
My obsidian armor, then powered down and thin as paper from the onslaught of reanimations is cleaved in two, Cadence immediately perishing under the mighty blow.
I will now begin talking about my opinion of the game:
I spent 20 hours trying to get farther and farther than before.
Being able to dance with the Necrodancer was an incredible experience, despite dying, my body is still flowing with music high. Please try this game. There are very smart design choices evident throughout every aspect. The music, the level design, the enemies and items all progress so well. Timing each act to the length of a song, having enemies which all have simple but broad ranges of dance moves to overcome make them easy to approach but brilliantly challenging in hoards. You feel extremely rewarded for your experienced-earned dexterity the roguelike demands--the game is a fantastic challenge that's never too easy.
A great example is in certain circumstances (secret vendors and trapdoors) do you find yourself in an incredibly confined space with two minibossess and two small minions. The first time you see this your fear and greenness lead to your immediate demise, but after enough of dancing do you begin to, not only feel comfortable with these, but even actively seek them out for the item and gold reward from defeating them.
Once you can beat bosses, your greed begins to demand you defeat them without a single misstep, for the glorious Flawless Victory that rewards your ego as well as giving you an additional chest to bolster your hero. I thought being an indie game this would be a quick fun change of pace but it's so much more. I've only played twenty hours but I don't intend to stop any time soon. It's a game I would recommend to any friend who comes over, it's a game I would play when I have a short break or if I have a few hours. Sometimes it can be tough if you keep dying but the rewards essentially beg you to succeed.  I keep coming back for more Crypt of the Necrodancer!

This is by far the worst Lego game you'll find. I can barely even quantify the reasons its bad, it just is. The models are uglier, the jokes are either nonexistant or sexist, and every single segment you go through seems to be something thats designed to kill you for no reason.
The other Lego games have thought put into them. The puzzles are made for kids, but they're still puzzles, and the level design is usually just as charming as the visuals. This game just fills boring-looking rooms with 30 respawning droids and asks you to put one thing together while they're shooting at you. Its a pointlessly annoying video game.
I got to the spaceship section and immediately uninstalled. The controls were sub-par (even given how hard they are to mess up with this kind of game) throughout the rets of the experience, but that level was just unacceptable. You get knocked and jitter every way but the way you're going, and if you even look at a wall you go flying in a random direction. There's *something* shooting at you, but you have no way of knowing how to avoid damage.
These games are made around forgivingness. The worst penalty for dying in these games is just losing money. But the awful frequency at which the game just decides to be terrible and fill a section with unavoidable damage is incredible. There's almost no penalty for dying, but because you never feel like it's your fault, each death just feels like an insult.
Buy the other Lego Star Wars games. Buy any other Lego game. This is the last one you should even consider.

Like many, Iffy on if to recommend this.
Right off the bat, im not interested in sabotage mode. Solo and coop is what I want - If I wanted pvp, id go play eve or something.
My biggest complaint is many of the higher teir maps turn into "go put out this fire over here" with barricade destroyers, 4+ lanes to defend, bosses, Mercenaries, Rift portals... Some of these, if you miss it, you lose on a 20m+ map right at the end because the RNG killed you buy spawning two things you HAVE to do now or lose. This makes coop mode feel significantly easier. Personally, I feel that barricade destroyer minions should be significantly nerfed (especially in solo. In a wave of 200 orcs, the ONE tnt archer can ruin the whole map and cause you to loose with a single shot), and would like to see more single (or limited/combined double) lane maps.
Yes, Progression is slow, but not painful imo. But, I dont mind slow progression. Your milage may vary. Outside of sabotage I dont think its really nessisary to pay up, but the starter bundle is a nice boost to grab a couple of chars (and get that infinite use guardian potion!) and rack up a healthy amount of skulls in the first week.
Balance feels a bit out of wack at times (partially due to damage increase/reduction based on account level, and some just unbalanced heros) and a couple of the maps are simply unfun. Certain chars are clearly better than others for solo vs coop game modes, mobililty and income being absolutely critical, with damage output a definate consideration. ``tank`` chars dont feel very important from what ive found. For coop, Three players feels better than two, due to monster scaling.
Being limited to 8 traps per player is also pretty annoying for solo play. You have a few auto-take traps, and a lot of traps I would like to play around with end up collecting dust due to this limitation. In coop each player can take 8 traps, so I would like to see solo and duo modes increase player trap count (say 12-10-8, or something)
One of the biggest pros is ive found several chars I quite enjoy playing. The increased roster is actually imo a pretty huge selling point for the game. Unlocking the skin you want for those chars, however, is utter BS (1 in 34 chance from a $3 chest - If I could just pay 5-10$ for the skin I wanted I might, but im not going to drop $100+ on enough rng rolls for it.)
Id have to say that as a solo game OMD 1+2 were better, if shorter, experiences. If you want more, then this is worthwhile, and being f2p its not costing you much to check it out. Im not done with it yet and 100+ hours is pretty damn respectable for a game to hold me that long. Expect to loose some maps, and have to figure out the map, wave composition, and ideal traps and chars to use for it.

I mostly play this on PS4 since my PC is kinda terrible with this game, but I'm going to try and be as honest and impartial as possible (the latter of which can be a tad difficult due to my first point). I'll dedicate this review to the two worst and two best details about the game since I sometimes drone on.
BAD:
-It's a F2P game. If you don't already know what that means then the short hand explanation is that the game is a hard slog through tedious repetition and hours upon hours of grinding. The genuine rewards are few, far between, and not often worth it since it is difficult to know exactly what you are working towards. Even worse is when you get it and find out it isn't your cup of tea.
-There are many balancing bugs that can make the game somewhat unplayable unless you have two friends who know the game and have leveled up enough to be of use. Multiplayer can often seem impossible due to no coordination between team members and the fact that enemies seem to triple in health when faced with 3 players instead of 1. There are some harsh difficulty spikes and many of the characters feel underpowered compared to others. Admittedly that might just have to due with practicality of skills in certain situations or playstyle differances (but turning into a nova bomb as Smolder is clearly better than doing less basic attack damage as Ivy while occasionally rooting enemies for 1.5 seconds)
GOOD:
-The voice acting is high grade due to the stellar cast including Robert McCollum and Colleen Clinkenbeard. This can make the characters much more likable. This game is more of the same which is fairly great news to those of us who have played the previous installments and enjoyed them.
-This game can challenge you if you enjoy solving puzzles and strategizing with a time limit. I have often found myself playing a specific map several times in a row simply to find the best way to set my traps and force enemies down the longest path while I funnel them into my line of fire.
To put it bluntly, the game is decent, but if you want to play a fun defence game with quirky humor while slaughtering legions of moronic orcs... just play the first two.

My first impression was "Star Hearthstone", and I wasn't completely off. Personally, I was not a fan of the "feel" (artwork and music) of Hearthstone, but I attribute that to the cartoonish nature of WoW itself.
The gameplay is fairly quick, depending on decks used. There are a few issues I noticed, several which I read are being adressed in future updates-
Matchmaking- It can get severly imbalanced at times, but I haven't run into too many issues.
Timers - Timers count down and board control simply switches to the opponent. I had a match where a player ran the clock down intentionally, so I did the same. We turned a simple match into an hour long staring contest.
Scrap- To create a common, it takes 10 Scrap. When you scrap a common, you get 1 Scrap. You literally need 10 extra (more than 2, although you can scrap any cards you wish) cards just to create a singular common. While it creates demand for in-game purchases, I believe the ratio needs adjusting.
It's not a bad game, and I will continue to play it. At least until the company gets sued and forced to shut down.

The gameplay works well too, both driving (especially with the recent tweaks), stealth and weapon handling.
It runs smoothly at max settings with my GTX 1070 (but have also tested it it with a GTX 960, and there's room for improvement in performance).
NB: (I haven't tried any of the DLCs. Been playing 64 hours with little time spent outside missions, both optional and story. Once that's done, I don't see much more to do.)

I really don’t know if i can recommend this game. :-/
Everything is more fun with friends, and that is so for this game too as usual.
And if you are willing to pay i have no doubt you will have a more fun time too, the more you pay the more the fun you have i imagine.
Even then rng may, i imagine, back stab you with the unlocks.
As a free to play person, so far, i can tell you the grind is real.
Currency to unlock traps and chars, and lvl up the traps with cards and currency.
And loot chest grind from other useful unlocks that i do not think you can actually pay for in the store for.
Like a amulet that makes traps and barricades takes less damage if you are close to them.
(if i heard and remember it right)
One of the both pro and cons of the game is the amount of traps and heroes.
If you are a free to play person i imagine you will never get any of the other cool ones (get perhaps one), and if you pay, you can get every hero for 30 euros.
But then you got the currency grind, and you can get it by playing, or paying, but the amount you get and the amount you need is silly large.
If you are free to play, hope for good daily deals to fill out your trap load out, and focus on a single few traps, as you will in NO way get enough currency, and cards to get em all far up the trap level tree.
Now the grind.
Almost all the maps have multiple entrances and with some few map exceptions they can not have one kill box.
Aggravating indeed if you try to single play em.
No doubt you can with good traps, right hero and youtube to help you out.
I can not say that it is fun tho.
With friends you will breeze thru the lower “challenge level” with 5 stars on all of em in no time.
There are also endless and weekly challenges that you can enjoy as a group.
Solo, not so much enjoyment.
Some maps revisits on the harder challenge levels, but have fun trying to guess a proper load out before you enter with the bare bones gray map as a guide.
And there after your memory to help you there, because we all love how we can not see stuff there, right?
Now for more cons.
Forget both breeze and proper load-out if you pub.
So far as i know, it is random which map you get when you wait for a game, but challenge level is set as you look for games under that window.
If you dare being slow, make a mistake or being inattentive you may get the usual, non friendly “banter” like “i am gonna report you, i am gonna sell all your traps, learn to play noob” and the rest we all come and love from pub games.
(thats after you have set up so your team mates can sell your traps if you made a mistakes, or if they have something better to place, trap lvls are a thing after all)
You don’t loose the credits, and you can place stuff else where you think?
Well, be prepared for the “helpful” person follow you around selling and putting up the cheapest thing he can till the 50 trap limit.
Other times you get nothing at all communicated, and it either goes great or not.
Some times there are actually helpful players who actually tell you their plans and what the team can do to make it awesome, but thats so rare i think i have only have it happened twice.
Or yet other times,  players may get disconnected or stand in spawn and do nothing whole game.
The chest rewards can be great, or for a mode you really should not play till you are max rank.
Same with the three daily quest, they can also have the same requirements.
Play sabotage for x reward, or kill this random boss that you have to google to see if you can find and beat.
Sabotage is a versus mode.
And apparently levels and unlocks matter allot, so good luck getting invited for one before lvl 50.

**Pros**
-Beautifully rendered city environment
-Great soundtrack
-Offers a variety of tactical choices in combat
**Cons**
-Shooting gallery AI
-Dull and repetitive missions
-Weak plot
Mafia III is like a selfish lover - it starts fast, climaxes early, and then rolls over and goes to sleep. After starting by throwing you into the action and quickly progressing to the game's dramatic turning point, it never gives you any compelling reasons to keep playing. Lincoln's quest for revenge after his betrayal is boring, implausible, and mind-numbingly repetitive.
The missions have little to no variety: kill, coerce, and destroy, in unchallenging and uncreative ways. There's no emotional urgency or tactical challenge to any of the laundry list of tasks that Lincoln is obligated to complete in order to advance the plot. They feel like delaying tactics to avoid progressing directly to the game's final showdown, instead of elements of a tightly woven narrative.
That's really a shame, because the game has a lot of promising elements that could have been made into an extremely compelling story. The atmosphere of social and racial tension that forms the backdrop of the game is portrayed in a pretty nuanced and thoughtful way (Dixie Mafia and voodoo dolls aside). People on the street freely share their opinions of the social and cultural upheavals of the late 60s, and their observations are generally authentic to the period. The talk radio programs also do a good job of exploring the polarization that existed during the period. And the sights and sounds of New Bordeaux are truly immersive. There are beachgoers, Mardi Gras revelers, heroin addicts, and a whole array of small touches that makes it feel as if you're truly moving through an inhabited city. Unfortunately, the story line fails to do its setting justice.
If Lincoln had been forced to conceal his identity and gather information on his own, slowly revealing the elements of the conspiracy that led to his betrayal, the game's narrative tension would've been much higher and the missions would've been more satisfying. Instead, the game introduces an old CIA buddy who's just completely out of place and irritatingly cartoonish. His sole purpose is to chain smoke and give out information that advances the plot through exposition instead of action. He may as well have been named MacGuffin. The only contribution his presence makes to the game is unearned information, deathly boring cutscenes of congressional testimony, bad acting, and goofy wiretap sidequests. It's an idea that should've been cut out the game entirely.
-GAME MECHANICS-
On normal settings, the AI will occasionally try to flush you out and flank you, but for the most part enemies will generously comply with staying in one spot and repeatedly sticking out their heads for you to blow off. Enemies will also offer themselves up like lambs to the slaughter when Lincoln ambushes from cover, repeatedly walking into the same trap despite the five foot high pile of bodies in front of it. Lincoln also has the ability to pick up and move bodies out of sight, in order to remain undetected. The cover mechanic is a bit wonky, making it difficult to move quickly from cover to cover, or to pick the intended cover in the first place, but given the AIs general incompetence, it's not that much of an issue. The ambush from cover mechanic is one of the more satisfying tools in the game, but as I mentioned earlier, it can be exploited because the AI will never avoid sending waves of enemies to the same ambush spot.
Despite the array of tools that Lincoln can be outfitted with, from molotov cocktails to proximity mines, combat overall is pitifully generic and unchallenging. The wide variety of heights, interiors, objects and landscapes that the game renders so meticulously are never fully exploited. Every encounter is a shooting gallery.
Shooting, driving, running and climbing all work pretty well. Bullet time is available, but the action was never intense enough that I even thought about using it. There's also a so-called "intel view" that gives you x-ray vision, and makes no logical sense.
-GRAPHICS-
New Bordeaux is beautifully rendered, with a wide variety of landscapes and neighborhoods on a sprawling game map. Many have complained about the game's poor optimization, but it runs well and looks stunning on my rig. YMMV.
-FINAL THOUGHTS-
Despite its lofty aspirations and beautifully-rendered setting, Mafia III's story and gameplay just never finds its footing, and it winds up lost in the bayou swamps. 5/10

Star Crusade is a collectible digital card game, and my first few days have left me with a very good impression.
The first thing you will notice is how similar it is to hearthstone. I know everyone else has mentioned this, so I will as well. There are many things borrowed, and that can be good and bad.  If you play hearthstone the game will be instantly accessible and comfortable, with a few different powers and keywords to learn. If you are looking for something different, you may find there is enough of a difference to give this one a test, especially if you are not a fan of the RNG, as so many are not. This game shares some elements of hearthstone yes but it is trying to cut its own path.
The graphics are hit and miss, the menus are only OK and the backgrounds are mostly static, but some of the art is absolutely amazing. Some of the cards look like they come right out of an old buck rogers comic or HR Geiger exhibit depending on your race. Some are a  little bit not good (pulse rifles, you need to change right now) But mostly, I really enjoy the look and feel of the game.
The matches are fast and furious, and while starting out the game can be daunting (the first many matches/few days will be harrowing as you build your collection) due to the fact that many people you will be matched with will have much superior decks/know how to play, if you stick with it you will be rewarded with a game that has deceptive depth. The amount of keywords, cards and configurations in the first set is rich and rewarding. Is it as deep as hearthston? not quite, but that game has been out for years. I honestly think this is a much better game out of the gate (and in beta) than hearthstone was when it first launched.
Over all I highly recommend giving this a shot and sticking through the first few missions to grab a few of the rarer cards and trying to learn the ins and outs of the game.

If you play games for the game play mechanics, then you might like this title. Dust: An Elysian Tail is a 2D platformer with a lot of somewhat simplistic fight system. The main character has a sword with a few basic combos. Fidget, the main character's companion provides spells. Spells can be combined with sword attacks for some powerfull combos. These are all unlocked as the story progresses. There is a leveling system with a max level of 60. Each level provides the player with a stat point to put into one of four stats (Attack, Defense, Fidget (magic spells), and Base HP). In my experience, leveling was pretty quick and did not require any grinding. The main character has equipment slots that can be filled with either store bought or crafted items. Currency is obtained by killing enemies and also by selling loot. The crafting system is unlocked at a certain point in the story, and blueprints for the items are randomly dropped by enemies. Enemies also drop the materials needed to craft the items. Once the player sells a material to the vendor, the vendor will start to stock that item from then on. This helps to avoid the need to farm materials.
If you play games for the story telling, then you might like this title. The story begins with the main character having no memory of who he is. As the story progresses the player and the main character discover his identity and his relation to the ongoing conflict. I felt that the story was compelling and interesting up until the very end. The voice acting is done very well in my opinion, and I think that the dialog is great as well. Most of the characters were interesting as well.
The world and character design in this title are very good in my opinion. The cartoon style is bright and colorful. Animations are quite good as well. Most of the enemies are non-humanoid monsters, and the few humanoid enemies are portrayed as being evil.
Overall, I really enjoyed my time with this title.
