I decided to buy this game sometime in May last year because it was on sale and that is when I saw it for the first time. I was sceptical that it was going to get boring after the first few hours or that it was not going to be fun at all, but it turned out to be my best 5€ purchase ever and one of my best purchases in general. This is literally the game I have been the most addicted to and the second best gaming experience I have ever had (right after my experience playing TF2 and R6S).
The game is simple and easy to pick up, but if you're addicted like me and play it that  much, you will come to the realisation that there are always new tricks to learn, from the different strategies you can use on each of the original maps, to learning how to shoot diagonally upward and downwards, jumping 5 and 6 blocks of height (you usually jump 3 or 4), learn all the exploits and glitches in the game, learn how to play the instruments and become really good with the timing of the grenades.
It really is a silly game that most people wouldn't dig deep into and would just play to mess around, but trust me, there is much more fun stuff to do besides the core gameplay, you can even play tennis by reflecting a quad laser with a sword!  It has two really convenient options: the quack button (that you use to be a jerk and taunt people) and the ragdoll mode (you use it to act like you're dead, but it's really useful when it gets to mobility stuff since you can jump higher or escape from some nasty situations).
What else can I say about it, it's brilliant and it's super addictive and fun, I don't think that anyone would regret buying this piece of art, it doesn't matter whether they are going to get really into it or just play it for a few hours with friends when they are bored. If you get bored from the original maps,  there are a plenty of community made maps and mods, so it will always feel fresh, whatever you do!
Should you wait for a sale or no? Personally, I think that this game is worth every single cent of the original price, but if you are not sure whether you're gonna love it or not, wait until it's on sale.

It's a must-buy in my opinion and an experience that everybody would enjoy.

Digging into this for 50+ hours, I belive I feel ready to sum it up.
There has been lot of criticism compared to Mafia II, so let's go through ti one by one.
1) No, it is not your regular italian ''Cosa Nostra'' story, no sharp dressed Sicilians (Napolitanes), no more of a family like crew or omerta - it's different. This is likely the main reason the game received such reviews - those who expected another italian story were dissapointed.
2) Optimalization and graphics - this piece will pretty much juice your hardware, even GTX 1080 with i7 is lucky to make it over 70 fps. Still on my i7 2600 with Gigabyte Radeon HD 7850 OC runs smoothly enough. However without top hardware simply forget about higher details. As to the visuals in general, there are some glitches - blurred screenes, poor reflections, ocassional flaws like objects stuck one into another (car wheels, doors, enemies in walls - but it is not too common), further - sun reflections and weather effects - day/night switch, sunny weather in general are not very well done, but I managed to get into the story so much I didn't care. Still, visuals are lovely anyway, especially spectacular !! design of New Orleans, especially French Ward and Downtown are fantastic - how about the hippie den in one of your rackets ? :)) - and except for a few pieces, animated sequences are great with some of the best facial animation I have seen. Beats Mafia II most of the time in my opinion. Especially Cassandra can be quite persuasive at times.
3) Story - it's a revenge piece of black mobster going after the Marcanos when they crossed and finished his black ''family''. Gameplay of slowly taking down of the Italian empire can get repetitive, although some side missions may spice it up. But then The Godfather (2004) and Scarface were basically the same and I still enjoyed them, especially playing for Tommy Montana and hell, that game was sure repetitive. All the time the same, just take one district after another.
So if you played those, you know what to expect.
Story in general is well written, and despite being a simple revenge story, the 60's setting in the Deep South amidst the revolutionary times of Martin Luther King more than make up for the game's shortcomings.
The basic line here is - don't expect a Mafia game. This is more like GTA free world game, and if you take it as it is, and get into the 60's atmosphere of racial, social and political changes, the story will really step up as a gem.

So, this is my first hones review on Steam.
When I first look at the reviews, they were mostly negative and that influenced me that i stoped playing this game for about a year. Now I have finished the game and can write the review.
Mafia II was the game that got me into franchise. Mafia III is different game, there is no so much attention to details (e.g., running water in the sink, opening the trunk of a car, or closing a fuc***g door), but those were the things that existed in previous game, which were there for show-off, not like anyone used them... So puting that aside:
GRAPHIC - graphic are good, smooth with 60 FPS, glichy at some times, but not game-breaking.
GAMEPLAY - some reviews say it is repetitiv, always doing the same thing over and over, while it is true, you are doing the same thing over and over in different district, and every district has its own boss which has unique way of killing him (e.g., plant a bomb, pursuit through the amusement park, mask as a servant, etc.). The gameplay is not boring and has many sidemissions that can be done for each of the underbosses. There are also racing minigames which are spectacular if you buy expansion with extra vehicles (which is really cheap). Also, the game has 4 or 5 different endings to explore. Collectibles dont unlock anything, but they are fun - Playboy, HotWheels, and that religious magazines are readable with original content and album covers are true to the source.
SOUNDTRACK - OMG the soundtrack <3
CHARACTERS - Some characters are redundant, but characters as main bosses, your underbosses, padre, Donovan - they have great development, through conversation and through the cutscenes which are breathtaking. You can see how each of your underbosses react when the district is given to someone. While this game features Vito from Mafia II, he is not in the focus which is not really the problem, because Lincoln is one bad mofo.
CONCLUSION - this game is not Mafia II and should not be compared to Mafia II, this game is a decent continuation in the Mafia franchise, it features some of the characters from the previous games, but only for the flow of the story. If you like gangster theme, great soundtrack, interesting combat mechanism (takedowns, authentic firearms) and badass cars - buy this game!!!
FINAL SCORE - 8.5/10 (not the best game there is but surely among them)

I feel like most reviews don't actually focus on balancing this game's ups and downs properly, both the positive and the negative ones. The positive ones overvalue what people perceive as "cute" while the negative ones bash the game too much. There are a few reviews that make a justified description or review of the game. Obviously I'm not doing any side a favor with this. I'll explain why I can't recommend this game after stating a few facts about it. Keep in mind I'll be taking in consideration the price of the game and what the game offers for that value.
- Cutscenes and Artworks for some in game events.
- Movement is fluid.
- The overall style is cute.
- Small optional interactions you can do in the game to make yourself feel more involved with the story (such as poking Leo when he sleeps because why not).
- Multiple endings.
- Lack of consequence if you do certain mistakes;
- The lack of actual places to explore per chapter makes the game feel repetitive and boring on the long run.
- No combat depth despite being advertised as a JRPG. Additionally, if you grind some levels you can actually become immune to damage, including boss damage.
- Despite being advertised as "A fantastic JRPG focused on storytelling." the storyline is very short and doesn't hold up to that statement. The story is appropriate for the price of the game. Don't get your hopes up.
- Some in-game designs for characters are poorly made (especially the artwork of characters on the right of the dialogue).
- The in-game money you acquire is useless.
For those interested
, I'll start off with the
:
1. I didn't expect any type of cutscenes at all. I thought it's just some trailer animation. It was a nice surprise. It makes it easier to imagine what's depicted or how the characters actually look in an RPG viewed from the top.
2. For this price I had some feelings that movement speed or the FPS cap would be an issue. Good thing I was wrong. The movement is fluid and fast enough for the size of each map.
3. While it doesn't captivate me as much as others, the style is chibi-oriented and cute.
4. The small and sometimes meaningless optional interactions you can do does make it, at least for me, a better way of appreciating the game, rather than not having them at all.
5. It's great to have multiple endings to slightly personalize the story depending on some actions you do. Some might argue that a linear great ending would be better rather than branching out.
Now for the
:
1. The moment I saw Lies that you can battle I immediately thought of "hey, this looks like a nice detective game! Maybe if I pick the wrong choice, it's gonna affect the case or make me redo it...or at least lose a certain amount of HP". Sadly it doesn't expand on it and there's no consequence with failing to find the lie(s) (unless you count the fact that you waste some time on some battles)
2. Being used to JRPGs, I expected more zones than what it has. There really isn't too much to explore. But for the game's price I can't really complain that much.
3. If a game has "JRPG" or even "RPG" as its genre, I expect some combat depth and some grinding. Sadly the only part where I had to "think" was in the first chapter where I used an AoE attack to get rid of a line of mobs. Overall, you can just keep mashing the Attack option and still win. And if you reach a certain level with your characters you become immune to damage.
4. The storyline is okay for the price attached. I really wish there were more scenes and more character development because I wanted to get to know some characters more than the game allows me to. I spent some time in RPG Maker. Adding text is not that hard (And yes, I do imply this game was made in RPG Maker or something similar). But like I said before, for the price I paid, it's not a big issue.
5. There's a lot of pixelation done with the characters in the artwork shown on the right of the dialogue, such as Leo looking way too low quality compared to others and not too appealing to the eye. Maybe that's just me, I don't know.
Why do I not recommend this game? Because it could have been something awesome like "To the Moon" or "Ib" with enough hardwork and patience. I would buy the game at a 5-10 euro price tag if the game was focused on the following:
- More places to explore
- More optional dialogue and interactions with the characters
- Expand the combat by adding some strategy to it
- Most importantly: Make it a detective JRPG game where I interrogate people and find the truth about the case.
This game had the potential to be a JRPG focused on finding the culprit and solving mysteries. Not to the lengths of "Danganronpa" or "Ace Attorney" series, but at least give more player input and consequences related to uncovering who done what they did. It has a dragon loli who can detect lies, for crying out loud!
I'm not gonna go into details on how this could be made as everybody has their own ideas of how to improve the game. However, I really wanted some negative effects if I'm doing something wrong with finding lies, make me find who the culprit it according to clues and then give me the option to accuse someone. Heck, maybe use in-game money you acquire to buy hints.
The artwork is okay, the BGM is okay, the story is okay, overall this game is average. And that's the problem. I really wanted to recommend this game but I can't. And it's not because of the value of the game, it is for what is worth. It's because it could have been something awesome and unforgettable giving the right time, patience, hardwork, and price. Yes, I'm not recommending this game only because it wasn't polished to its fullest potential. I wanted this game to be awesome (with an appropriate price for its greatness), but the dev team decided to stop and deliver an okay game for its current price.

I am aware that the reason for not recommending it isn't truly justifiable. From an objective standpoint I'd recommend this game. But this is a review with my own personal opinion. Thus, a subjective point of view is more appropriate.
A message to all reviewers who keep saying stuff like "omg that girl is so cute and you should buy the game because of that!": You are overvaluing the "cute" aspect of the game way too much. Is it really that big of a thing for a dragon loli that discovers life to be this game's selling point? Or the artstyle? Because I don't think so. Maybe that's just me. Who knows.
A message to all reviewers who say this game is "horrible" or bash certain aspects of the game in an exaggerated manner: don't forget you spent 2 to 3 euros/dollars on it. For that value, don't expect too much out of it. It's not gonna be Final Fantasy. As mentioned above, the game is neither good or bad. It's average. If you're that disappointed, just sell the Trading Cards you get from it and compensate some of the money you spent. If you're lucky enough to get a Foil type of Trading Card, you can sell that for at least the amount of money you spent on the game.

There isn't an RPG I know of that has held such charm and innocence above it's rather darkly surreal world like LiEat. You play as Theobald Leonhearts and his dainty companion Efina through 3 games, each taking place after one another. You follow them through 3 different settings each one sprinkling you bite-sized bits of Theo's and Efi's personality and past while foreshading a deeper meaning to your adventures. Each game plays the same way only differing in story and setting so the game will be evaluated in a general sense.
Soundtrack
The sound design in the game works well but isn't anything special at all. It gets moody or bright when it needs to be. Overall the music seems to give off the feeling of bittersweetness which is fitting for the game.
Gameplay
The gameplay here is what you expect of an RPG with a little twist where you can decide if you indeed want to engage or not in combat beased on being given an option to decided whether or not a lie is genuine or not. This makes the combat pretty much optional save for the bosses and the few unavoidable fights. However the ending you recieve can be determined by your character level but unfortunetly the enemy scaling is really bad. All the enemies save for boss characters are lies in a physical creature-like form and it is possible to get strong enough to destroy the bosses by grinding on the weakest enemies.
They just give you way to much exp and this becomes more apparent each game the first being the most balanced in my opinon. I also find it odd you get money too but never use it for anything. The game progresses for the most part by speaking with characters or checking objects in a sequential matter which is sometimes boring to be honest. Sometimes this leads you to pressing 'Z' on everything you come in contact with or searching around far too long. This also led to me finding the legendary weapons in both the 2nd and 3rd games which was pretty cool because they were hidden invisibly but they really break the game and I don't recommend even picking them up unless you just want to enjoy the story. In the second game you can find the legendary weapon on the second screen right at the beginning which is very unfortunate but the thrid game fixes this.
Overall the gameplay is fine if a little imbalanced and sometimes mundane. It seems comfortable not taking the idea of deciding which lies are genuine further than a plot device rather than a real  fight mechanic. I liked that Efi follows you like Pikachu would in the old Pokemon games but was dissapointed that I couldn't turn around to converse with her.
Story
The story is the meat of this game in my opinion but it sure takes it's time selling you on it and I really felt like most of it was in the 3rd game while the other 2 were just primers for the big drop. It's not the best but not the worst and once I was learning more about Theo and Efi I definetly wanted more and the game delivers well on that part. This game contains interesting lore where dragons are born with human appearences and each with a special ability and it delves a bit into the idea but often I found that the abilities were pretty lame. For the most part the characters you engage with are interesting and have a personality that is acceptable but they are mostly forgettable. Sometimes the dialog makes no sense given the context an example of this is the responses you get from the maids after completing the investigation on them in the 3rd game. The most enjoyable moments here are the interactions between Efi and Theo.
LiEat is an RPG mostly centered around it's story and the relationship between the two main characters. The combat is almost optional and could use some work to balance out. The settings could be better since the 2nd and 3rd game's are too similar. It is thematicly cute feeling but keeps a dark and surreal tone when it comes to the plot devices which was pretty neat. Overall it is enjoyable but rough around the edges at times. You can tell if this game is going to be enjoyable for you almost immediatly. I say follow your gut on whether or not you want to play this one because it is an experience that is varied but what is appealing about it very apparent and doesn't stray far from that.

Graphics
The art design is what you would expect from an RPG Maker game however LiEat sets itself apart from the others with it's brief animations which are usually used to introduce a character for the first time or during key events. The static images that are sometimes used instead of an animation in these sequences are okay, they usually feature a character posing cooly. My only gripe here is the character portraits that appear when one of them is talking. They are cool looking but are harsh on the eyes to make out the smaller details in them.
For me this was a 6/10 slightly above average but could have been a 7 if the game had a little more strategy involved in the combat it was just too much of a breeze. I enjoyed it in parts but didn't in others but I'd still recommend becasue the price is very fair for what it offers.

Here we have an odd one but a very good odd one. For starters, the game looks like an RPG but it could practically be a visual novel. It has the entire RPG coat of paint with stats and equipment and such but none of it really matters since there's almost no fighting. You actually aquire equipment faster than you can use it and collect more restorative items in one playthrough than you would need for 10 playthroughs. In other words, it's all about detectiving and the story.
You play a conman/detective who is a habitual liar and also as a young dragon who looks about 5 or 6 but is actually just a year old. Said dragon eats lies but she can't eat Mr. Conman's lies since the person has to admit the lie and she has to know it's actually a lie before she can eat them. So this game has 3 chapters and with each new chapter the duo move to a different town where Mr. Conman dons a new identity and they have a new mystery to solve. It's all well-written and interesting.
There are some flaws, though.
First, in Chapter 1, there was a point where you had to identify lies and clues were hidden in the area to help with that. I thought that was cool but it turns out that sort of mechanic was not really used after that. It would have been nice to have that mechanics used a lot more and in more clever ways. A lot of the time you're just guessing, the answer was spoon-fed to you or it's a "clean up the lies" segment where everything is a lie and you don't have to worry about getting it right.
Second, TINY TINY window. If there's a way to run this game fullscreen, I never found it. Not even Alt+Enter works. The game normally runs in a 640x480 window.
Other than that, I would highly recommend the game. All three chapters can be done in 6 hours or less but for $3, that's still a good deal.

Completionists, stay away.  There are things that are practically impossible to obtain.
Roguelike purists, also stay away.  The game mechanics aren't extremely deep.
Otherwise?  As long as you can tap to a metronome (or at least learn to) and do enjoy action, I highly recommend this game.
Crypt of the NecroDancer, at its core, is a rhythm-based action with roguelite and dungeon crawler elements.  People have compared this game to games such as Faster Than Light and Spelunky; I really enjoyed the former and felt iffy about the latter, and after 350+ hours, I don't know if I can really stop playing NecroDancer just yet.
It's very easy to pick up and understand the core gameplay; one or two local players act to the beat (with only the arrow keys), and everything else responds to your movements on the same beat, allowing you to plan for the next beat.  Getting dropped into the first zone after the tutorial level, you're introduced to a small variety of items, learning about this and that, buying and picking up things to figure out what your favorites are, and dealing with a small variety of enemies.  Items definitely make things easier, but it's absolutely possible to finish everything and low% a run with only default gear.
(By the way, if you want to have a sense of genuine curiosity, go into the options and disable "show item hints".)
And once you inevitably die, it's not so bad.  There's almost always a way out of whatever predicament you managed to get yourself into, and you sensibly chuckle at it and figure you'll do better next time.
You slowly progress, saving a few unfortunate NPCs from cages, buying new things with diamonds and slowly expanding the pool of items you get to find and use during runs.  You finally manage to get the boss down, start to learn why Cadence is in this dungeon of dance, and then you're back to square one, figuring out the patterns in the completely new world that is Zone 2.  And you work through it, because holy crap is that Danny Baranowsky soundtrack fantastic and motivating.
And you keep at it.  Some things change completely, some things don't, and some things get flipped upside-down and force you to change tactics.
Occasionally, you take a break from Cadence and pick up a different character.  Oh yeah, there's other ways to play the game in Zone 1 again, and some new strategies for enemies you've seen before.  All the normal characters are interesting to work with in their own way.
Once you feel that you've finished the important stuff, a variety of things open up.  Score runs?  Speedruns?  Sure thing, try to see how well you can do on the boards and in the daily challenge runs.  Low%?  Go for that, if you want to.  In terms of replayability, you get about as much as Spelunky -- everything generally stays the same, but for some reason the variations between runs always gets you coming back for more.
Mods are a thing, to some extent.  At the very least, many resources can be replaced and custom levels are supported and supported through Steam Workshop.  That's about it, though; there's no way to add in completely new items and content just yet.
Remember what I said about completionists?  Yeah, if you want to 100% this game legitimately, forget about it.  The developers added in a character that even they think is impossible.  There's absolutely nothing except bragging rights and an achievement to gain from completing a run as said character (unlike in, say, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth), so you're not missing out on too much otherwise.
It's been great watching this game only get better from Early Access; Brace Yourself Games has been nothing less than incredible with regular development and responsive to the community.  If you haven't been driven away from reading this yet, it's absolutely worth more than the $15 that it's listed for.

Personally, even I don't know why I'm giving this game a negative review. Maybe I'm just spoiled on what Lego Star Wars: The Complete Saga already delivered...
Naaaaaah!
Lego Star Wars III- The Clone Wars is the next game Traveler's Tales was contractually obligated to make from Star Wars, before they'd lose the rights, which I'm sure they're refreshing with their new release for The Force Awakens. And, as always, there's a problem with the Traveler's Tales Lego games that seems to have started with this entry...
Traveler's Tales doesn't believe in patience. At all.
Why wait for us to do a complete Indiana Jones, when we could release two? I know! Let's also release Lego The Hobbit within months of Battle of the Five Armies, but not include it in out game! Wait! I've got another idea! How about we make Lego Star Wars: The Force Awakens, before the other two entries are even made!
It's sad, honestly. I really like certain elements of LSW III that I do like. The new characters and locations inspired from the Clone Wars film and TV series are all fun to play as, beautifully animated, and great to control. There's tons of new abilities available, allowing tons of new opportunities for puzzles, such as mnigun targets, grappling, and precise Force movements.
However, this feels like a really shoddy attempt to give these new abilities so light to shine in. There were a fair share of puzzles in the original LSW games that didn't outright tell you the answer, but you could figure them out with your own deduction skills. But with the way the puzzles are set up for the new abilities, it's always obvious what you have to do next.
On top of that, if Traveler's Tales had waited for the ENTIRE series to finish its run, they would have had a lot more opportunities at their hands. Hundreds of characters, tons of new planets to choose from, and even more abilities you could create.
But it really feels like they chose the most boring planets to visit. Out of all the levels I played, I only liked Ambush, Rookies, Lair of Grievous, Hostage Crisis, and Castle of Doom for their aesthetics. 5 out of about 25 levels. Because most of them are either space levels, running around dark, metal corridors, or battlefiels in the middle of a desert.
Where's the snowy tundras of "Trespass"? Where's the swamps of Rodia from "Bombad Jedi"? The massive fungal world from "Bounty Hunters"? It doesn't feel like TT chose the most creative or unique planets from the show to focus on.
Along with that, I'm not the biggest fan of the massive battle levels. They might have been better in the match mode, but from the story mode, it's a very one-sided fight with some simple building mechanics, that would've worked better if you could select bases at once, instead of running to the base you want to build on, and then building there.
However, I did enjoy the space levels for their new enhancements to the original level design set up in LSW II. Now, you don't just fly around and shoot down enemies, you also can fly into cruisers, and take out individual droids and solve puzzles as a normal character. It has the Battlefront II feel to it, that I enjoy.
I also enjoy the new minikit feature, where they actually unlock different character to play as... but that leads into one of my biggest complains for the game...
The Hub. It sucks. It absolutely sucks. It's far too large. Everything is spread too far apart, so it's a drudgery to get to another side of the ship to buy a new vehicle you unlocked. Or if you forgot a specific character to solve a puzzle, you'll have to find another character-selector and then return to solve the puzzle.
I mean, hell, there's an entire space zone between the Republic and Separatist cruisers, if you want to go all the way to the other side of the Hub to unlock the villain characters. In layman's terms, this sh** is spread too far apart.
And while I do like the new minikit feature to unlock character, I don't like the lack of creativity spent in hiding the minikits- especially in the battle levels. It gets so predictable, that it gets flat out boring to collect all the minikits, or frustrating if you make a small mistake, and suddenly a section of the level is blocked off and you'll have to reset (but you can save what progress you've made- which I do like).
I'm giving Lego Star Wars III- The Clone wars a 5/10. It's a massive mixed bag filled with tons of new things I like a LOT... but a ton of other things that felt like Traveler's Tales was just going through the motions in making another Lego Star Wars game. It's not bad, per se, but it doesn't have enough good features to make it distinguishable from the rest of the Lego video game library.

Not in love with this game at launch.  It's not a bad game.  It just isn't exceptional.  Ship building is bugged currently.  The game itself froze up on me a few times but after a fresh install seemed to run better.  It still stutters at times, even on the small tutorial map.  Combat is uninteresting.  You have no capacity to command your units, not even to flee.  So you send your guys in and hope for the best.  Worse, the combat camera is fairly horrible and you spend a lot of the time listening to battles happening off screen.  It's a bit chaotic.
I have read that diplomacy is a greatly improved in this game.  If so I didn't see it.  In the two games I have played so far my allies seemed fairly erratic, almost like a crazy person you find yourself dating after an online hook up.  One minute they threatened to obliterate me for not following their doctrine.  The next minute they are showering me with credits as though they feel badly about how they acted and are desperate for you not to leave them.
If there is colony management automation I couldn't find it.  Managing your economy is a matter of moving a slider.  Again, not bad.  Just not interesting.
The Universe in the couple of games I have played seems fairly lifeless.  At first black holes look really neat.  But there are no civilian ships to be seen.  No convoys.  Besides some basic animation of a moon orbit or the odd comet it seems like you are looking at a stagnate game board.  Again, not bad per say.  Just not interesting.
Towards the end of the games I found myself clicking a lot to just shuffle through turns so I could finally get to the tipping point of overwhelming my enemy.  This involved stripping his final system of defenders and then doing a sort of auto resolution troop invasion.  Then a wall of exposition and a victory screen.  It was around this point that I realized that finishing the game had been more work than actual fun.
There may be a solid core of a good game here that can be greatly improved upon with further patches and DLC.  But for $10 more you can buy Distant Worlds Universe.  With a bevy of mods that make it a living breathing universe.  Or just play some Gal Civ 2.  Or Sins of a Solar Empire.  I do not recommend dumping $50 into Gal Civ 3 at present.  It needs a lot of work.

As someone who is new to the series I was initially impressed with the game and I still am to some extent however there are rather griping issues that are bugging the hell out of me currently.
Ill try to list them:
1) the tutorial is not useful. Instead of it being about teaching new players or existing players about new or old mechanics and how they work and how your colonies work with production, manufacturing etc. it is instead used as a story spring board ready for the campaign.. which I really do feel like it should be for teaching as you know it is supposed to be a tutorial, Of course it has information on how things work but doesnt accurately explain it, in other words its extremely vague.
2) Lack of audio communication from Characters. When talking to another race for example, or something your research scientist is telling you about your recent upgrades. I really do feel like if they added some decent voice overs it would bring a ton of depth to the game. I realise many of the old school GC players would not like this that much is clear from what ive read on forum posts concerning this however its a different time now and you need to expect that immersion is important and right now Voice Acting even a little goes a long way, nobody wants to sit their and read paragraphs upon paragraphs while playing. Adding voice acting + a on/off option would solve this anyway. I believe the campaign would benefit heavily from some voice acting immersion. instead of "oh look we're retaking earth lets click our way to victory yay". I have a fine imagination I can imagine voices for the characters but it really doesnt do them justice. in a game this big and this well known they deserve a bit more "soul" i guess would be the correct word.
3) Clarity concerning modifications to your ships and fleet "military research". While most of the research details you go through are fairly solid and easy to understand, things like ship hulls and shield strength and how much it actually adds on to your ships current shield or hull strength isnt carried over and communicated properly making things seem tedious and confusing as if your research something for no reason because you dont understand where it goes or what it does fully. Examples would help this or fix it. I appreciate the lack of hand holding in the game, but again for games to be popular in the current industry they need to accomidate new players not just the old ones. Which is why many feel that the game has not innovated on what had come previously.
4) Governance is ...outdated. Frankly with competition like Civ and others in the mix Governance is an expceptionally dull part of an otherwise enjoyable game. I personally think if they wish to rival Sid's civ games then they really should of though about going a step further than they have or maybe a few steps. Instead of giving a player a set ammount of tiles you should of been able to zoom in and actually build upon the planet you found place your city yourself and the various things you need to get production and influence going etc and by that I mean actually control workers to do thats etc and have way more than simply under 10 or 20 tiles per planet or even under 5. I realise that many will use the arguement of "but its not trying to compete with it" or whatever however companies no longer have a choice these days unless they want to make money and frankly the changes ive suggested are hardly anything that would harm your experience if anything it would improve it. What had so much potential seems squandered.
5) Space battles. When launching real time battles between fleets its abundantly obvious that the battle viewer is extremely underdone, ships consistantly fly out of view..the free cam movement is extremely redundant as moving seems almost a chore rather than something you can enjoy as you watch your fleet tear the enemy apart, its clear that this needs to be dealt with and frankly if it isnt, it will be something that ruins the game.
Conclusion:
A game with enormous potential but fell short of it due to being stuck in the past, the graphics are updated and its new enough not to be called a "reskin" based on what ive watched from other videos of GC II HOWEVER this game is stuck in its own past. Instead of innovating they simply stayed still all be it with a few side steps on a couple of things which I personally think is what destroyed my opinion of this game. Now its still possible a lot of the things ive mentioned will be changed or fixed so I will give this game a little more time but this game is far from what stardock hope to achieve which apparently is "The largest, most advanced, strategy game possible.
Verdict?
Not recommended, especially at £30. As I have said while I largely enjoyed this game It frankly just did not hit the marks it needs too in this current day and age, Im glad a game is trying to stick to its roots but if a series is to improve itself it must go forward and not be stuck in the past, I will continue to play this game and try a bit harder to enjoy it though frankly if it was a decent game for the era I would already enjoy it thus I wouldnt have to try.
What is starteling is im finding im enjoying Beyond Earth more than this and thats for one reason:
Depth. Now I know what your thinking "Beyond Earth, Depth? Don't make me laugh" but frankly its true if theres one good thing you can say about that alpha centauri mess up is that at least they tried to make the game at least seem like its got a bit of soul. While GC III does a great job of making the galaxy look beautiful (to an extent) and letting you decide what you want your civilization to be it losing out massively on the things ive listed perhaps bar number one as a tutorial shouldnt be the focus of a whole game. Until they add voices and more depth and explainations as to how things work in game by providing an in-game source and fixing the various new features to actually work properly I cannot actually immerse myself in this game not can I call it a good game beyond a simple "meh its okay". if you prefer the silent type and unnessasarily complex mechanics in games then this game is for you if you prefer much more immersion and a bit more ease so you can just have fun without having too feel like your reading a book rather than playing a game I would advise you not buy this until that changes. it is stuck in the past and frankly its sad, it has so much potential but falls quiet short of a great game in my opinion.
Clearly Stardock have put a great deal of effort into the game but they got too focused on "sticking to the roots", you can stick to your roots and still evolve your game, however it seems they had no idea how to beyond improving a few small things and improving the graphics thats about it.

Orcs must die franchise is very popular for the single player element, previous titles have had co-op. Unchained adds a   new genre defying pvp element called sabotage. The core is similar to previous titles but the cash shop is the big elephant in the room.
I have played many games that had a cash shop from pc to mobile and I wouldn't favour the direction and pay to win elements  currently in this game. (You can buy a potion for skulls -in game currency- or gold -Cash-  that increases damage by 50%) Sabotage favours end game max level players to spend currency on so many different consumables.
I understand skins, or emotes. All the base content is free however which is nice but you will need to grind out currency or buy heroes, no "try before you buy" option here. I was dissapointed with the three heroes I did buy. My two other friends that I got playing this game and purchased starter packs played tanks, and they are much better than me. You cant exactly buy all the traps you want you have to unlock much harder difficulties and have a "chance" of getting the trap, then you slowly gotta upgrade that trap 7 times to be effective.
The core gameplay element everyone enjoys doesnt come soon enough, as you level you get chests, grind, slowly unlocking more traps. There are actually a lot of traps to choose from and some benefiting certain champions. unfortunatly you will be building Spike pits and arrow walls for the first 20 or so levels. 2-3 days. Overall gameplay is very smooth everything is solid things get REALLY intense in survival.
TLDR: So do I recomend this game? well, if you don't mind a bit of grind and a free game that has a bit of pvp.  go for it! Or if you wanna have more fun off of the bat. Go for the other orcs must die titles

You have to get logs from a lumber camp to an objective using Russian trucks in lots of mud. I know. Sounds sh*t. Yet one of the most awesome coop simulation games I've ever played.
The mud physics - out of this world good. Carelessly spinning your tyres in an over-powered gear makes it even more difficult for the next load because the road state is actually faithfully persisted across the map. The engine modelling: the diff-locks, manual gears, AWD - tough to properly master but so accurate you could probably drive a dirt-track lumber truck in real life with ease once you do so. The coop aspect - the delights of spending half an hour pulling a fallen comrade out of a river in the dead of night with a winch, only to see them fall in again (pulling you in too). And the overall challenge - you're fist pumping the air once you manage to finally get an objective completed on hardcore.
10/10 would spend 2 hours driving through 6' of mud to deliver 12 logs again and again.

Digging into this for 50+ hours, I belive I feel ready to sum it up.
There has been lot of criticism compared to Mafia II, so let's go through ti one by one.
1) No, it is not your regular italian ''Cosa Nostra'' story, no sharp dressed Sicilians (Napolitanes), no more of a family like crew or omerta - it's different. This is likely the main reason the game received such reviews - those who expected another italian story were dissapointed.
2) Optimalization and graphics - this piece will pretty much juice your hardware, even GTX 1080 with i7 is lucky to make it over 70 fps. Still on my i7 2600 with Gigabyte Radeon HD 7850 OC runs smoothly enough. However without top hardware simply forget about higher details. As to the visuals in general, there are some glitches - blurred screenes, poor reflections, ocassional flaws like objects stuck one into another (car wheels, doors, enemies in walls - but it is not too common), further - sun reflections and weather effects - day/night switch, sunny weather in general are not very well done, but I managed to get into the story so much I didn't care. Still, visuals are lovely anyway, especially spectacular !! design of New Orleans, especially French Ward and Downtown are fantastic - how about the hippie den in one of your rackets ? :)) - and except for a few pieces, animated sequences are great with some of the best facial animation I have seen. Beats Mafia II most of the time in my opinion. Especially Cassandra can be quite persuasive at times.
3) Story - it's a revenge piece of black mobster going after the Marcanos when they crossed and finished his black ''family''. Gameplay of slowly taking down of the Italian empire can get repetitive, although some side missions may spice it up. But then The Godfather (2004) and Scarface were basically the same and I still enjoyed them, especially playing for Tommy Montana and hell, that game was sure repetitive. All the time the same, just take one district after another.
So if you played those, you know what to expect.
Story in general is well written, and despite being a simple revenge story, the 60's setting in the Deep South amidst the revolutionary times of Martin Luther King more than make up for the game's shortcomings.
The basic line here is - don't expect a Mafia game. This is more like GTA free world game, and if you take it as it is, and get into the 60's atmosphere of racial, social and political changes, the story will really step up as a gem.

It's made clear from the very beginning that The Witcher 2, while definitely inspired by countless other games, exceeds in nearly every level, taking only the genre's best bits and weaving it together in an impressive world that will without a doubt amaze you.
The universe is rich with life, from the natural beauty of the game's diverse landscapes to villagers doing anything from chatting together by a campfire to taking a♥♥♥♥♥♥discretely on the side of a cabin. I describe the core gameplay as somewhere between a Bethesda game in the RPG department and a Zelda game in the Action-Adventure. It's not a complete open world like Skyrim, but it's structured similarly to Zelda. There is customization, emcumberment and skill trees, but there also is wonderful combat, a fantastically-woven, malleable narrative, and somersaulting.
Yes, you can somersault in this game. Somersaulting makes you go fast and you can get upgrades to make your somersaults even faster. If you've ever played a 3D Zelda game before, you will be right at home.
The graphics deserve a nod. This game is ridiculously gorgeous, and only help to sell this interesting world to you. Prior to playing this game, I had no idea who Triss Merigold or the Scoia'tael were, but now I certainly do, and that just through playing the game, and not through some Lore book or Wiki. The world is so interesting that you just pick these things up naturally as you play.

So, this is my first hones review on Steam.
When I first look at the reviews, they were mostly negative and that influenced me that i stoped playing this game for about a year. Now I have finished the game and can write the review.
Mafia II was the game that got me into franchise. Mafia III is different game, there is no so much attention to details (e.g., running water in the sink, opening the trunk of a car, or closing a fuc***g door), but those were the things that existed in previous game, which were there for show-off, not like anyone used them... So puting that aside:
GRAPHIC - graphic are good, smooth with 60 FPS, glichy at some times, but not game-breaking.
GAMEPLAY - some reviews say it is repetitiv, always doing the same thing over and over, while it is true, you are doing the same thing over and over in different district, and every district has its own boss which has unique way of killing him (e.g., plant a bomb, pursuit through the amusement park, mask as a servant, etc.). The gameplay is not boring and has many sidemissions that can be done for each of the underbosses. There are also racing minigames which are spectacular if you buy expansion with extra vehicles (which is really cheap). Also, the game has 4 or 5 different endings to explore. Collectibles dont unlock anything, but they are fun - Playboy, HotWheels, and that religious magazines are readable with original content and album covers are true to the source.
SOUNDTRACK - OMG the soundtrack <3
CHARACTERS - Some characters are redundant, but characters as main bosses, your underbosses, padre, Donovan - they have great development, through conversation and through the cutscenes which are breathtaking. You can see how each of your underbosses react when the district is given to someone. While this game features Vito from Mafia II, he is not in the focus which is not really the problem, because Lincoln is one bad mofo.
CONCLUSION - this game is not Mafia II and should not be compared to Mafia II, this game is a decent continuation in the Mafia franchise, it features some of the characters from the previous games, but only for the flow of the story. If you like gangster theme, great soundtrack, interesting combat mechanism (takedowns, authentic firearms) and badass cars - buy this game!!!
FINAL SCORE - 8.5/10 (not the best game there is but surely among them)

Hearthstone. In. SPAAAAACE!
But in all seriousness, if one hasn't already guessed from the screenshots and other reviews, it's so mechanically similar to Hearthstone that it may as well be a reskin. If that fact already turns you off from the game, I don't blame you. A lot of what you'll see in this game is something Hearthstone already does, but with far more polish. Hearthstone is by far the more developed game compared to Star Crusade, and Hearthstone doesn't take itself nearly half as seriously as Star Crusade does. It's not a
game, but it's difficult to judge Star Crusade on its own merits when much of it is so heavily borrowed from another game.
However, that's not to say that Star Crusade doesn't try to mix things up a little. Where there are obvious similarities, if not downright carbon-copied mechanics/classes with different labels --I'm looking at you Terran(Paladin) and Hierarchy(Priest)-- the game does try to introduce concepts you won't find in Hearthstone like Criticals, Mutate, Soak, Armored, etc. Some mechanics are not very well-explained, though, and tend to be up to the player to figure out (Criticals insta-kill, I think?) and in a CCG, not knowing what your or your enemy's cards do in the middle of a game is
.
I will say that I'm having fun with the game so far, unpolished as it is. It's certainly worth a try for the novelty of playing a Hearthstone-like game with some different features you won't find in Blizzard's own CCG. Ultimately, it's hard to say if Star Crusade is really trying to be a good alternative to Hearthstone, or if it's a cynical 'follow-the-leader' cash grab hoping to net some Blizzard fans.
For now, I give it a tentative recommendation, if only for novelty's sake and the fact that it's free, but if you're looking for a Hearthstone 2.0, this probably isn't it.

Released on iOS in 2012, and Steam in 2014, About Love, Hate and the other ones is an underrated should-be classic. And by underrated, I don't mean "a game I like that no one else does". Most people who play it love it. It's won several awards, and for good reason too.
So why am I reviewing it now? Because it deserves an audience.
This is a puzzle game, not in the sense that Tetris is, but in the sense that Lemmings or Toki Tori is. Just like Lemmings or Toki Tori, your goal is to figure out ways beyond obstacles en route to an exit.
But of course, there's a twist. You control two characters:
Think of Love as the character that "pulls", and Hate as the character that "pushes". And you'll be doing a lot of that because NPCs will either help or hinder you from getting to your goal.
As for why they're trying to get to their goal? They pressed a red button, and now they're trapped in a place far away from home and must find their way back. As with many puzzlers, the story isn't so important.
What is important is how accessible this game is. It will appeal to many people. Moms should love this, and toddlers should love this. In fact, my toddler very much loved this, and it held her attention for quite some time. It's an easy to understand puzzler that is equally easy to pick up and play.
This neither utilizes polygon nor pixel art. Instead, it opts for what looks like hand-drawn art with a mix of charcoal and watercolours. This gives it a style that resembles children's book illustrations.
The graphics for this game look amazing. The kicker is that they don't require horsepower. This is a case where art really does make a statement. The style is whimsical and fun, and is easy to love.
You don't need a whole lot of optimizing to enjoy it. I've run this game in resolution as low as 640x480, and as high as 1920x1080. In an array of configurations, it looks great.
The game uses music at the main menu and loading screens, but when you actually play it, it opts for ambient sounds. Which is fine by me because when I'm playing a puzzler, I like to have room to ponder.
As far as effects are concerned, they mostly accentuate an action. When you move, there's subtle footsteps. When an NPC does something, you hear a pop.
The most noteworthy aspect of the sound is when you get your characters to attract or repel. When Love attracts, it says, "I love you." When Hate repels, it says, "I hate you." Adults might find this slightly annoying, but I assure you that kids think it's pretty cool. In the event you don't like it, the game gives you the option to turn off the sound without turning off the system sound.
This is as simple for a PC game to control as it gets. You don't use a keyboard. Everything is driven by the mouse and left click. There's never a point in which you require a right click.
Would you rather play this on a couch with your Steam controller? The default right trackpad and right trigger emulate a mouse perfectly.
That said, there are issues with control. In order to get a character to interact with an NPC, you have to click the character then the NPC. Yet sometimes instead of interacting with an NPC, your character walks towards it. This is annoying because it sometimes results in your character getting into a bind. Thankfully, the game gives you the option to undo, so it's never too much of a hassle.
Certain gamers may roll their eyes at About Love, Hate and the other ones -- deeming it too "casual". But if by "casual" they mean "accessible to nearly anyone", guilty as charged.
Besides, if you were a PC gamer back in the late 80s/early 90s, you might be thirsty for a game similar to Lemmings. I'm happy to say that this, along with MouseCraft, shows that this style of puzzler is still going strong.
If you're around children, here's something that will keep them entertained for hours on end. I hate to use the phrase "family friendly" because those are usually weasel words for justifying dreck, but here's a game all ages will enjoy.

The Mafia series of games has always been one of my favorites ever. First with Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven, one of the deepest and richest linear stories ever, then to Mafia II and its faster-paced yet still poignant and affecting tale... Now to Mafia III, which has gone open-world at last under the tender hands of Hangar 13. Have they succeeded in bringing Mafia up to the next generation?
Mostly, I think yes. As far as open-world games go with the Mafia storyline, it succeeds. You definitely don't feel as railroaded, that's for sure. There's quite a lot of things to do in the New Orleans-esque New Bordeaux, most of it having to do with crushing nefarious Mafia Don Sal Marcano's criminal empire, but there is also racing, (with the added DLC) bounty hunting and horticulture and even the restoration of a prominent city landmark.
The game is not entirely bug-free. It still stutters at 30 or 60 frames per second even after being updated a lot; there is flickering of the geometry every so often, and some things may not happen the way you expect unless you exit and re-launch.
Still, for what I played of it (which is most of the content including the entire main story; past a certain point all the repetitious activity (the aforementioned horticulture and bounty hunting) does lose its appeal), it is very awesome and I enjoyed it immensely. Check it out on sale as I did! :)

A rhythm-rougelike game that is incredibly fun to play.
Besides being a rougelike game, it doesn't give you time to think your next move, because every move you make is bound to the beat of the dungeon, which features the catchiest soundtrack ever.
This creates a mixture of strategic jumping, frantc battles and trying to smack your enemies around to the beat (which is surprising satisfying, though might get you into trouble if you aren't carefull).
The mmucis is really good, and besides it there are two more soundtracks for two characters, if you wanted more (one is synth remix and the other is a heavy metal version, for the harder charcters).
There is a handfull of other characters you can play, some play difrent, but most are just plain harder to play, for those who want some aditional chalenge (and most of them are relatives of the main character Cadence and have music-pun names).
The enemies are unique and well designed, you can easily tell what kind of enemy is approaching you, and as you play, you wil get used to knowing what enemy is behind you just by their sound.
The shopkeeper is a retired badass like in most rougelikes, but also happens to be an opera (shopera) singer, which is really usefull as you can her him across the level, signaling how close to the shop you are. If you manage to kill him you get a bling crown that doubles all your coin drops, but his gost might come to avenge him in later levels.
If you like to play rougelikes to the beat this is the game for you (and if you don't want to be rushed, play as bard and play the turns as slowly as you want, while still enyoing the awesome music).

I decided to buy this game sometime in May last year because it was on sale and that is when I saw it for the first time. I was sceptical that it was going to get boring after the first few hours or that it was not going to be fun at all, but it turned out to be my best 5€ purchase ever and one of my best purchases in general. This is literally the game I have been the most addicted to and the second best gaming experience I have ever had (right after my experience playing TF2 and R6S).
The game is simple and easy to pick up, but if you're addicted like me and play it that  much, you will come to the realisation that there are always new tricks to learn, from the different strategies you can use on each of the original maps, to learning how to shoot diagonally upward and downwards, jumping 5 and 6 blocks of height (you usually jump 3 or 4), learn all the exploits and glitches in the game, learn how to play the instruments and become really good with the timing of the grenades.
It really is a silly game that most people wouldn't dig deep into and would just play to mess around, but trust me, there is much more fun stuff to do besides the core gameplay, you can even play tennis by reflecting a quad laser with a sword!  It has two really convenient options: the quack button (that you use to be a jerk and taunt people) and the ragdoll mode (you use it to act like you're dead, but it's really useful when it gets to mobility stuff since you can jump higher or escape from some nasty situations).
What else can I say about it, it's brilliant and it's super addictive and fun, I don't think that anyone would regret buying this piece of art, it doesn't matter whether they are going to get really into it or just play it for a few hours with friends when they are bored. If you get bored from the original maps,  there are a plenty of community made maps and mods, so it will always feel fresh, whatever you do!
Should you wait for a sale or no? Personally, I think that this game is worth every single cent of the original price, but if you are not sure whether you're gonna love it or not, wait until it's on sale.

Poor execution to this installment.
I don't like the game after whole Saturday of playing. Below are the reasons:
- no spying;
- units are not getting experience;
- money is not a problem anymore;
- diplomacy does not make any sense - they throw money at you for no reason;
- the worst part in my opinion is the planetary buildings - not enough space for anything and the idea of mutual interaction is lost due to lack of neighbouring to each other hexes;
- cannot balance the planets to ones needs - it does not matter what you are building it's going to grow anyway;
- lost variety of planet sizes - most of them are between 9 and 12;
- spaceship movement is not tailored to the game - the ships are moving 3 hexes, quick tech and they move 6 or 7 hexes and then very long time very little improvement - if you are playing insane size map or enormous military conflict is impossible - due to this civilizations are like mushrooms growing next to each other - fleet will have very little effect on gameplay because it takes forever to assemble the fleet and take over these measly 3 planets and then some other race starts the war with you and to move the fleet takes forever...
- I have quite good rig and time between turns is like a minute of computation (on insane size) - I go to kitchen set up kettle, turn, go to kitchen set up cup, turn, got to kitchen pour the water, turn, go to kitchen cut a slice of banana cake, turn, ... damn how many tees can you have?
- military conflict does not mean anything - if you started good and are focused on colonization by the time you meet other players you probably have already won because you have 48 planets and the second best civ is just 23 or you are going to be swallowed by the civ which is already 4 times bigger than you (that's what happened to me on insane size and challenging difficulty)
Generally game shows very poor balance and lack of options which were there in GalCiv 2 which I am going to stick with for some time now till they improve overall experience.
Game is simply not finished.
Edit1:
It seems that theyu are close to finishing the game.
I still lack spying but the game play is much smoother and more reasonable.
What i find to still to be fixed is:
1. The power graphs and computation of strenght of your faction.
I mean I have strongest economics and I am close to first in research which results in high end ships and high logistics fleets. Although I have much less ships than other factions the power calculator does not take into account that I have real ability to destroy any invading fleet. Which happened with Thalan Empire being (according to calculator) 3 times more powerful than I was in terms of military. In 10 turns they were reduced to next to nothing with one massive fleet of 10 tweeked destroyers - Thalans couldnt get even through the shields...
The real problem is that there is a diplomatic consequence to these silly power graphs. The factions are less reluctant to enter into agreements or aliances and in some instances they are likely to agree to partitioning of my faction.
2. Money or resource allocation became more of a problem but still for example it costs a fortune to improve a small tier spaceship in comparison to building improvements on the surface. I think it would be better to drop the price significantly and employ necessity to dock with a starbase for implementation of improvements. I know it is a game but it looks silly when you splash the cash and your tiny fast scout becomes a powerful but slow carrier behind enemy lines just in one turn. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.
3. Building the planet stuff is never ending upgrade. Which is good but... in order to be effective one you do terraforming and get extra tiles you need to actively attend the planet surface to execute most efficient layout. No problem on tiny maps. But when you go to huge or insane it becomes dull excercise. I have to admit I never applied a governor - just afriad it will make a mess out of the planet.
4. Lack of spying.
The good:
1. The new tiles system seems to work better now. Or it might be just me. I admit it gives another dimension to the game.
2.The ship designer is brilliant. I don't know what to change or add. Perhaps... new technologies like spy modules to steal technologies or destroy planetary improvements in times of peace or incite revolts/add to influence of chosen faction or... now I'm drifting.
Wishes:
1. Spying.
2. Battles could have orders like choosing tactics or formation, if not turnbased like in Endless Space.
Only so much this time. I play it more than GalCiv2 now.
Edit 2.
On higher difficulty levels AI is simply cheating. What a total dissappointment.
The other concern is - economics sucks. There is no reason to build anything else than manufacturing plants. One can convert manufacturing into money and science so easily that there is no point building anything else. Building morale buildings is pointless too after few discoveries.

I tried OMDU during the beta with my friend... as other reviewers have mentioned, it was a rough start. Maybe we're just die-hard fans of OMD2 co-op, but we decided to try it again after the full release.
Robot really did listen to their community. The PvE Survival mode feels a lot like the classic OMD experience now. Several design changes from OMD2 also keep the gameplay fresh, like guardians, co-op up to three-players, a cast of heroes with fixed loadouts and selectable upgrades during matches. I stick with Survival mode, but I see strategy discussions about the Endless and Sabotage modes and the weekly challenges.
The free-to-play model is definitely different. Probably slower, sometimes a little less convenient and more frustrating, but not really predatory (from my experience). Like OMD2, you're rewarded for winning maps, but now it's with currency and loot boxes. The loot box RNG can be entertaining, but also annoying for unlocking specific traps/upgrades/guardians/perks. Otherwise, most of the gameplay-related unlocks can be purchased using earnable currency -- I've unlocked many of the heroes without spending any money (to be fair, my friend bought me the starter pack). The starter heroes are still fun, and Max is still one of my overall favorites to play.
Other reviewers have made many of these points, but I'm chipping in due to all the mixed reviews. Hopefully you'll find that OMDU has plenty of maps, a lot of good content and a few gameplay updates from previous OMD titles, along with its... "different" f2p progression model.

As a big fan of the OMD franchise, i felt the need to write a review about the latest release from Robot Ent. I also feel that this game doesnt get the love it deserves. The devs listen to player-input and actually act on it.
This game was already out on steam before it's release, and i was hesitant to start playing it as i generally avoid playing games pre-release. Plus the fact that it got bad reviews didnt help either.
Well after 300+ hours in, i can safely say that this is the best f2p game i have played. Not that i play many f2p (hardly have any in my library) as they are the devils poop, but still.... If you want to throw cash at it (like i did with the starters pack) you can, but it is not needed at all. Everything can be obtained without spending a dime, it just makes it a bit more grindy.
It has the same feel as the original OMD games, but it is not OMD 3 (this for all the reviewers that cant review a game on its own, but keep comparing apples to oranges).  There are several playmodes available like Survival, Endless, Sabotage and since the recent patch 2.2 Chaos Trials. Also there are Weekly Challenges that throw a certain objective at you, like f.e. "Use these set of traps on this map to complete the challenge". You can play these modes as a group or solo. I wont go in detail about all the different modes as you can read up on them or play em yourself, but i can say that all these modes add alot of variety to the game.
There is a decent amount of heroes (16 of the top of a head) you can tackle a map with and each hero feels pretty fleshed out for a "new" game. You can unlock heroes and traps as you progress through the game. After completing a map you get rewarded with a chest(s) which contains trap cards and skulls. These can be used to get a higher tier of a trap or you can buy a new hero with them. It might be a bit grindy for some, but i feel it is balanced. If you want something you have to put in some effort.
Overall, recommended!

OMDU is an underappreciated and often looked down tower defense game.
In the game, you choose a hero, and then pick a loadout consisting of various traps, consumables, and guardians to help you defend the rift.
There are many common misconceptions about this game. Do not let these other reviewers fool you.
The game is loaded with content such as a weekly challenge, a custom hand-made puzzle for you to solve with your traps and wits. It also features a survival mode, where you play against the orcs and defend for a certain number of waves. Endless, where you take endless waves of orcs, and sabotage a game-mode that is in a weird place.
Survival and Endless are the go-to content.
You can couple with up to 3 people per a party, and you and your friends will split all the gold 3 ways.(6k(starting gold) / 3(numberofplayers) = 2k each ) ( The gold used to purchase traps during the game ) This does not neccessarly mean that with 3 people the game is harder. The AI will send more orcs, depending on the players, You have 3 seperate people attacking, and each of you have 4 abilities. Despite this, the game can also be played in single player, where the orcs would spawn less and deal less damage
In short, the game caters to the experience depending on the number of players.
Sabotage is a strange mode. Much like a custom hero line war from Warcraft 3.
In this mode, two teams of three play against each other. They both try to defend the same rift, on a *mirror map*
thirty seconds before the wave spawns, the players take the time to choose from 3 random minions and spells to use ONCE during the wave on the enemy team. So a player gets one random minion to spawn, and one random spell to cast.
>the only interaction between the players is summoning different minions to strengthen the wave, and casting silly spells that cause effects.
These spells do multiple things, they can buff the minions, debuff the enemy heroes.
You can see the other players playing, on a minimap, allowing you to strategically time when youre going to strike
There is no direct PVP in this game, your hero will never fight another hero directly. There was a mode like this in the game originally but it got removed.
Chaos Trials are a recent addition to the family. A player gets the opportunity to play survival mode, but with a twist. random effects will be added to the game, before it starts.
Each time you win, you get more effects. These effects can be detrimental, such as higher costing traps, or positive, like slower minions. This is the most effecient mode to grind in.
TL;DR
Orcs must die is a tower defense game with over 200 hours of content. There is no need to pay for anything in the game, it is completely possible to get everything for free. The game is not P2W, but P2progress. There is no competitive aspect in OMDU. This game is very casual, and if youre seeking an experience such as that this is the game for you. It is very fun to play with friends and work together to solve puzzles, and the developers love their fanbase and release weekly dev streams. Don't let the steamcharts mislead you, this game is a sleeper.

The Mafia series of games has always been one of my favorites ever. First with Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven, one of the deepest and richest linear stories ever, then to Mafia II and its faster-paced yet still poignant and affecting tale... Now to Mafia III, which has gone open-world at last under the tender hands of Hangar 13. Have they succeeded in bringing Mafia up to the next generation?
Mostly, I think yes. As far as open-world games go with the Mafia storyline, it succeeds. You definitely don't feel as railroaded, that's for sure. There's quite a lot of things to do in the New Orleans-esque New Bordeaux, most of it having to do with crushing nefarious Mafia Don Sal Marcano's criminal empire, but there is also racing, (with the added DLC) bounty hunting and horticulture and even the restoration of a prominent city landmark.
The game is not entirely bug-free. It still stutters at 30 or 60 frames per second even after being updated a lot; there is flickering of the geometry every so often, and some things may not happen the way you expect unless you exit and re-launch.
Still, for what I played of it (which is most of the content including the entire main story; past a certain point all the repetitious activity (the aforementioned horticulture and bounty hunting) does lose its appeal), it is very awesome and I enjoyed it immensely. Check it out on sale as I did! :)

I've not yet wrote a review of a game but I feel like this one deserves a review! When I saw this game I had to have it! The graphics are extemely beautiful and luring and the over all gameplay is really relaxing and fun! I streamed this live on Twitch and my audience really seemed to enjoy how peaceful it was, but not to an extent where they got bored! The game keeps the player active at all times but doesn't ask for complete and utter consentration (meaning I could sit and chat without missing a huge part of the story)
As you explore the depths of the ocean you get to learn a few sea creatures names, although I'd would enjoy it if there was a better system for this, because it pretty much goes through every single finish in an area (as in all of them - not just the types) so finding out what certian types where was a little difficult and after 5/10 mins trying to find out the name of one fish gets annoying and I just moved on. I'd also love if it included the coral but I think that's just me being nit-picky :P
One feature that I really didn't enjoy, but did not ruin the game is what we called during our stream 'Floppy Diver Syndrome'. I played this with a controller and my lord was it difficult to navigate! I tried inverted and normal and both where extremely difficult to use. I feel like the controls should have been neated up a little as sometimes it's just extremely difficult to control the main character, making things take way longer than they should - this is literally the only problem I had with the game.
As for the story line, I won't give anything away but I will say that it was really mind blowing and went in a direction that I honestly was not expecting! Really well done and very touching towards the end!
Also, just as a final note - a few people have said do not play if you are afraid of the ocean - I am terrified of being underwater and easily get anxiety when a game requires me to do so... but this game was different, I don't know whether it's the fact that the main character can happily breathe underwater or if it was just simply the breath-taking graphics but my anxiety was only spiked a little during certain parts of the game and not to an extent that I didn't want to continue playing (which is normally what happens). So I'd go into this game with an open mind, if it looks like something you'd like to play but are worried about how your fear might affect you.

The Witcher 2 is a narrative driven action RPG by Polish developers CD Projekt Red. To be reductive, it contains a lot of action-like RPG combat and deep mechanics common to Bethesda games, but is also extremely narrative driven to the tune of something Bioware might put out.  Over the course of the game, much of the Witcher's many turning gears become an immensely enjoyable machine, though it jumps to a rough start and could use a more enjoyable combat system.  I did play with the Combat Rebalance mod, which allegedly makes the combat better; truly I think it just made it more trivial, but those may be two sides of the same coin in this case.
I started Witcher 2 having never played the Witcher 1, and generally not knowing what the game was about or how it worked.  Let me be blunt -- that is the absolute worst way to start the Witcher 2.  The game does offer an overall useless tutorial (if you have the Enhanced Edition), but otherwise it throws you right into a pretty hot mess.  Very little is explained in the way of combat mechanics, the many systems at your control (things like potions, crafting, magic abilities), and the context of the warring monarchs and their mysterious assassin which are central to its plotline.  Overall, it’s a little daunting to start.  That said, I highly recommend you persevere; lying on the other side is a huge payoff.
What makes Witcher 2 shine is the well crafted, incredibly epic story of politicking and sorcery.  What’s even more impressive is the dynamic way in which it is presented to you; very few games give you the sense of control over the story the way Witcher does.  The game is divided into 3 acts, and the second act can be completely different based on decisions you make in the first act.  You will start in a different location, have different characters to interact with, and different quests.  Even more impressive is that Witcher 2 does a good job of staying away from the typical good/bad archetypes; characters usually feel complex and your decisions almost always fall into a gray area.  It never feels like the game is pushing you one direction or the other; sometimes being the bad guy pays off...other times, not so much.
The plot itself is very interesting, though you won’t find anything revolutionary about it.  Voice acting is typically well done, which is good because there is a LOT of it.  At least half the game can easily be spent talking to characters and fleshing out the world in which Witcher 2 takes place.  Cutscenes are serviceable, but nothing extraordinary.  Like many games of this scope, much of the Witcher 2 lacks a certain polish -- the game certainly looks beautiful, but animations are often clunky and transitions are not done well.
Lacking the most polish, certainly, is the combat.  Combat in Witcher 2 feels mostly like a buffer between unlocking more of the story.  With the Combat Rebalance mod, parrying is automatic and after some initial struggle, I quickly learned to spam the same ability over and over again, accented by mashing attack and rolling around.  I easily beat 95% of encounters this way.  While you have a lot of options in terms of equipment etc., the majority is useless or unnecessary and I would have liked a little more variety in loot and spells.  I wouldn’t say the combat is outright bad, but it is certainly mediocre and not the highlight here.
Overall, while there is a lot to nitpick about Witcher 2, I highly enjoyed it.  It’s a beautiful game which offers up one of the most interesting stories you can find in the medium.  Decisions are impactful and rewarding, even if combat is not.  If you like Skyrim, or Mass Effect, and wish there was a game which blended the two together into a great PC game, look no further than Witcher 2.

Hunger Dungeon is a new game that does some things very right and some things very wrong.
The way the game plays is a simple battling system where you buy a few spells and weapons and then fight it out. I wouldn't say it's a MOBA. I'd put it somewhere under a beat em up or a fighting game more than a MOBA. You go through about 4 rounds of map, earning gold and raising your hunger meter, which will kill you if it depletes. On the last map, you need energy shards to attempt to power the exit. Only one person can escape and they will die to stop you. I like this system. It makes the ending very stressful when you the few remaining people team up to stop someone with four shards.
The developers have put in a system in which you only have access to four characters per week, with no way to unlock except for money. It's a poorly implemented way to make a f2p game give the developers money, and a little more work could've made them much more while not feeling like a scam.
The game balance is not all that great, and certain characters are too slow to accomplish anything with no redeeming qualities, or low damage with a chargable hit which makes him do the normal damage of every other character. There are also spells, and they equal the playing field quite a bit. I usually buy the item which increases Spell Damage by 40% and some spells every game.
In summary, if you like a good time with friends or a relaxing fighter without too much depth or thought, Hunger Dungeon is for you.
